entry.title: Build Week 15
entry.content:
Well the washing didn’t finish until midnight! We hung it for the second time then I was finally able to get to bed. Pete started cooking bacon for the potato salad for our dinner that night.

I got up around 8:30 and got ready to face another week haha

We had two Utes arrive this morning at 6:55 and Lukas in his truck at 7:01. I could hear them hammering away when I was in the Mudroom. Lukas headed out somewhere at 11:05 and came back 40mins later. I did my morning of work. At about 1:10 Pete got a call from Lukas saying Tim (the man who extended our driveway) would be arriving soon and could we come up for a chat. We got ready and headed up a few mins later.

The grass (well, primarily mud now) at the front of the house site was in a really bad way and Lukas was worried that trucks were going to have a really hard time accessing the site and some drivers might refuse. He’d asked Tim to come and see what options we might have for putting some gravel down. Although it was not the optimal timing, it’s not too bad for us as we were planning to get a driveway put in there anyway, so we can just start that process sooner and it won’t go to waste - after the build we’ll just have to tidy things up a bit more. We’ll probably have to dip into my savings to pay for it, as we won’t have enough in the shared accounts to cover this along with all the other stuff planned in the next couple of months.

Lukas also mentioned that he’d ended up getting our windows delivered to a place in town, as he didn’t want to leave them out in the elements and he wanted to get the roof on first.

Earlier I’d had a call from Manning Freight, as one of the lights we’d ordered had arrived - they wondered if we could pick it up from their depot in Taree or if there was a business in Gloucester they could deliver it to, as they can’t come to our address or drop it at the post office (I will be forever frustrated by this situation - it’s crazy to me that I have to pay for delivery and not actually receive the item). He realised there were more lights to come and so he said he’d call me back and I said I’d think about what we might be able to do.

We confirmed with Tod from CDKJ that we’d like to go ahead with the Kitchen, Laundry, Pantry and Storage joinery (but not the robes) and he would now pass things to Cassie for the drawing stage, and then we could catch up again. We enquired on rough timelines so we could perhaps pair that with the trip to pick up the lights, and he replied “Where is the build up to? Was it just getting started? I can’t remember. It will be about a week before your preims are ready, so maybe ill keep you up to date and make arrangements in the coming weeks.” haha ‘maybe’ he’ll keep us up to date?! haha Hopefully it will all be fine, he’s been really good so far.

We had a weird email from Westpac asking us to provide the “Construction certificate approved stamped plans” before they’d process the latest claim - we’d sent them way back when the loan was approved so not sure why they were asking again. Anyway, Pete sent them on.

I was wondering if we should contact Penny to check she was OK with making all the purchases we’d outlined, before the sales ended tomorrow - I was a bit worried we might miss out on the discounts. But Pete said to give her until tomorrow, and a little later she had emailed us - sounding like she was well on top of things, yay!

After the workers headed home, Pete did his drone shot and we headed up to check out the latest, at about 4pm. They’d started putting on some panels, and added a few other bits and pieces.

The poor topsoil was very torn up.

We had a laugh at ‘The Three Bears’ of ladders.

We headed over to the cows, and lots of the bubs visited today! One of them kept licking the front tyre (obscured in the first photo).

Back home we had a quick look in the garden - some more passionfruit flowers were out, so we tried to pollinate them. We also noticed one of the little pumpkins had finally detached from the vine, so we’ve taken him inside to rest with the others.

Pete’s City Edge sandwich extravaganza for dinner!!

Tue 30 Jun

The usual arrivals this morning at 6:44, 6:47 and 6:51.

Troy at Manning Freight called and said the rest of the lights order had arrived - he asked if I’d found somewhere to accept them in town and I said I hadn’t yet. I said we might be visiting Taree in the next two weeks and wondered how long they’d be able to keep the items (Pete had thought they could keep them for a while as they kept Issy’s mirror at Christmas for us for about a month) but unfortunately he said he could only keep them 7 days. I asked where he usually delivered to in town and he said the Tyre & Battery place in the main street - I said I’d check with them today and call him back.

Karissa our mortgage broker got in touch to let us know progress on the next payment - she’d also sent the requested doc on to Westpac again telling them we’d already provided it in March haha she told them to hurry up and pay or the builder was going to pull the pin haha she expected it would be sorted today now she’d put the wind up them.

I finished my day session of work and we got ready to head into town. First we got the cans ready in the big black tub and Pete strapped them in the back. When we got to the Return & Earn, one of the machines was full and when we tried to use the other one, it kept sending our items back saying they weren’t accepted (we tried 3 or 4 different types, which all work fine normally). Very annoying! Pete sent them a message so hopefully they’ll come fix it.

Next we headed to Tyre & Battery to ask them if they’d accept the lights delivery for us. We saw a few packages on the floor so we were hopeful. Well they kept us waiting for ages, and then a man finally came and we tried to explain the situation - at first he thought we were there to pick something up and he pointed to the packages, but we tried to explain Troy had recommended them and that we were asking his permission to have something delivered there and he adamantly refused haha it sounds like it’s all gotten out of control for them and they’re sick of the deliveries (he was probably exagerating but he said there were like 10 courier companies that drop things there) - anyway, it was a bit disappointing. We wondered who else we might be able to ask. We had a couple of places in mind but thought we’d try Gloucester Hardware first. Well Craig couldn’t have been nicer about it! He didn’t seem worried at all. After saying yes, he asked if it would be on a pallet, so didn’t even seem worried if it would be a big delivery. That was a relief. I called Troy with the good news and he said he’d deliver the lights tomorrow, yay!

Walked back down the main street - tried to find the charity shop which was having the sale (all clothes free today!), but they were actually up the road near the cop shop and were already closed for the day, oh well. Got a few items from IGA then headed home.

Driving along the Bucketts I thought I saw Tim, and wondered if he’d been out getting ready for the driveway work - sure enough there was a digger on the block when we drove past!

Got home just before 3pm - made lunch and checked my emails. We had an Annual Pest service reminder, asking if we’d like to align it with the quaterly station check in July for a discounted price (yes please!) Penny had also been in touch.

That was great news about the EOFY purchases being sorted!

Now it’s 4:15 and the builders still haven’t gone home, so we haven’t gone up for our daily squiz yet - hopefully we can fit it in before my 5pm nap hehe

We were able to go up at about 4:30. Here’s how it was looking -

They’d done more work on the roof support for the dining room and patio.

Next we headed to visit the digger and the cows.

Some of the bubs came right over to greet us.

One of them was being silly with the tufty grass hehe

The photo doesn’t do it justice, but there was an epic sunset.

Back home I had my nap before doing my evening of work, while Pete watched a movie. At about 10pm I had a bit of dinner and we watched a show.

Wed 1 Jul

It’s come to my attention that Pete has eaten 9 Paddle Pops in the last 3 days!!

The usual suspects arrived at 6:39, 6:46 and 6:53. The sky was pretty.

We had an email from Penny -

We’ve arranged to meet at 1:15 on Fri. Re: the next progress claim ($210K, phew!) we discussed with Karissa and Penny and all agreed it was better to wait for the current one to get processed then we’ll submit the next one straight away. Karissa said the valuation has been holding the current one up.

The first of a few gravel deliveries came at 11:55.

We headed in to town at about 1:30. Spotted neighbour Pete’s Ute on the Bucketts and waved, but it wasn’t Pete - Clarkey perhaps. He didn’t wave hehe

The Return & Earn was working today, so we were able to drop our load of cans off - we used two machines and had a race, and Pete was victorious with $6.50 to my $6 hehe

Had a quick look to see the state of the Share Shop after it was ransacked the day before hehe

Stopped at the loos to wash our hands after they got gooed returning the cans - Pete snuck around the side and scared me and I screamed - a lady parked just up the road was watching and must have been wondering what the heck we were doing.

We saw some Maggies and gave them some peanuts. Went by the dog park but there were no doggos and STILL no agility equipment - the Men’s Shed better get their act together!

Stopped at the Hardware store to pick up our 3 lights for the lounge room - it was so great they were able to accept the courier delivery for us.

Next stop Woolies to get something for dinner (we’re going to attempt to make our own Koftas) and fed some more Magpies.

Had a look in the pet shop - they’ve gotten lots of animals since we last visited - Budgies, Canaries, Quails, Chickens, Parrots. We said hello to all of them hehe We also bought a couple of small jingly balls to hang in the tree out the front, and some coconut husk stuff that we might be able to leave out for the birds when they’re next making nests. It should have cost $10.90 but he only charged us $10 - win!

On the way home we passed neighbour Pete’s Ute again - still not sure if it was Clarkey or not, but he waved this time!

Pete got a call from Mick and they had a long chat about the upcoming electrical work - he’d be starting on the 13th July.

We had a look at the new lights - they will be fine, but are not quite what we wanted (the dot holes are a bit too uniform rather than being oddly shaped like we preferred). We haven’t tried them with a globe yet, so that will be interesting to see.

My Waterdrop delivery had arrived and I made my first Apple drink with the cube - luckily it was delicious, as I have 72 of them to get through haha

I did some more work, then after the workers left we headed up to the house site at about 4:30. The topsoil had been removed and the driveway was starting to go in.

And here are the daily shots -

There weren’t too many obvious changes, except some work on the back patio. Pete got a nice shot from the main patio.

We also spotted someone had been walking in the crusher dust, I wonder who!

We headed over to see the cows.

A lot of the bubs were coming over, but we didn’t get to spend time with them today as we saw a lady walking on the road and she waved and started talking to us, so we went to say hello and the cows got a bit scared and ran away. The lady was our neighbour Gabi (not sure how to spell it, but it’s pronounced Gar-bee rather than Gab-ee) - she’s an older lady who lives up on the hill and she was lovely. She mentioned how she likes to introduce herself to the new cows and I can totally relate to that hehe I think her and her husband have lived there since 2011.

Back home I did a bit more work and then spent some time on the monthly finance recon - no big surprises yet, but I think there will be a few landing next month eek.

We were starting to get a bit low on firewood so I’ve ordered another 4 scoops - he’ll deliver them on Monday.

Pete tested out the new lights and then he made us some delicious koftas.

Thurs 2 Jul

Oh no, we forgot to have the greek yoghurt with our koftas last night! Oh well, I’ll just have to get Pete to make me some more on Friday hehe

We got the quote through from Cetnaj for the electical supplies Pete was waiting on - it’s all double-dutch to me, I don’t know how he works it all out!

In related news, Lukas has pushed Mick’s start date back from the 13th to the 31st, so hopefully we’ll have time to get everything. Oh, breaking news - just noticed one of the items is made to order and might take 4-6 weeks, uh oh!

Pete has been working on some fancy AI improvements for the house plans - maybe he’ll tell us a bit about them shortly.

V&B suggested a visit soon and we decided the 11th might work - we can meet in Stroud so they can see Pete compete in the brick throwing, before coming to stay the night. Mum and Dad might also visit later this month but the date is TBC.

Spent some time trying to decide what to do about the BYD build date issue - wrote to Fair Trading but not sure if they’ll respond.

Had an earlier site visit today as everyone had left by 1:40 - slackers! haha just kidding.

The main changes were more roofing for the back patio, and more driveway.

Now we were getting the feel for spaces a bit more, we realised the bathroom toilet room was quite large - maybe we should try to extend the bathroom a bit by way of an alcove for storage / shelf space - we were a bit unsure where we’d put things like shampoos as I don’t really want a shelf on the shower wall (I don’t want it to stick out) and an alcove may not work as the wall is too thin. But the side walls seem so far away so I’m not sure what will work best, we’ll have to think some more.

Although I have a great view from my new office, I was also a little sad that I won’t have all the birds outside my window anymore - well until we grow some new trees and shrubs for them at least.

Finally got around to planting the 3 chokos! Next to poles on the front fence. Pete then had to remap Looby a bit so he wouldn’t chop them.

I watered some of the garden and great news - we finally started growing a cauliflower!! It’s one of the purple varieties.

Spent some more time researching possible gifts to buy Laura - it was her 40th Birthday last week and she’s about to go on a big trip overseas, including a few days in Paris, so I thought it might be a nice idea to buy an activity for her. I found some pretty cool stuff, wish I could do them myself! hehe

Finally got my $30 Myer voucher through (for spending $150 last month) and bought some more undies - woowoo haha I hope Dad won’t be embarrassed picking them up for me from Castle Hill hehe

5:15 and time for a nap now, then back to work at 7:15.

It ended up being a longer work evening than expected and then I got chatting to Laura and organising her Birthday gift - we decided on the personalised 100ml perfume experience which she’ll take on the 9th July. She’s flying out on the weekend and will be in Paris for 4 days then Zagreb, Split, Dubrovnik, Rome, Amalfi Coast, Cinque Terre and Nice. I am very jealous!

Didn’t have my dinner snack until after 11, eep!

Fri 3 Jul

Pete chased Karissa about the progress payment again - it had been 12 business days now, which was well beyond the contract terms. Karissa called a bit later and said she had the bank on the phone and wasn’t hanging up until they’d paid! She said they were complaining that the plans we’d sent through were stamped but not certified. We all thought they were talking out their arse but we sent through everything AGAIN. Karissa called us back shortly after, saying they’d paid, but it would take about an hour for it to go through their system then we’d get an SMS with confirmation. Luckily it all went through about 10mins before we were due to meet Lukas and Penny for the site visit, so we were able to give them the good news.

We were with Lukas and Penny for about an hour and covered various topics including -

  • Lukas apologised for putting us on the spot with Tim the other day regarding the driveway - but we said it was fine as we had always planned to do it eventually. He was really happy to have it sorted already. We agreed Tim was great!
  • The pump location - it shouldn’t be a problem behind the battery shed.
  • Lukas spoke about the problem with the steel measurements, but we still don’t quite understand what went wrong. But Lukas realised when he was measuring everything that instead of the hallways being 1.2m they’d only be 1m - he managed to mostly sort things so now they’ll likely be 1.175.
  • We spoke about the layout in the dining hall wall/ceiling and confirmed Pete would be able to run his cable baskets - but we’re not really sure how the air conditioning will affect everything and we’ll need to speak to Chris.
  • We have a rough idea on locations for the external air conditioning components, but will defer to Chris.
  • Both patios are likely to have raked ceilings.
  • Mick and the plumber will work together to set up the hyrdronic heating - the plumber had recommended another electrician for Mick to speak to first who has done hydronic heating before.
  • We mentioned that we’d been reconsidering the bathroom/toilet space and considering a nook - they said it didn’t sound like an issue and we could work out the details when the time came.
  • Penny said one of the things we should start considering next is tiles - Pete and I actually were kicking ourselves we hadn’t thought to look at tiles during the EOFY sales, d’oh!
  • We spoke about the windows and we asked where they had said they would be stored, as I didn’t know we had any glass places in town - it was Zac’s Glass Service out on Clement St, which we’d driven past a hundred times and just never noticed haha they joked about the owner, who apparently people either love or hate. They said he’s the type of guy who can bend over backward for you, but also you will really know when he’s angry at you haha
  • Regarding the carport, Lukas said we had a few options for the support opposite the house, which was currently planned to be a beam across, supported by two brick columns at the ends. He was thinking we needed another support in the middle, but maybe not the beam across. And he wondered if we wanted to close the top triangle in. We said we’d have a think about it.
  • Pete told them about his fancy door hole / mortice plan - not something they’ve really done before (drilling all the way through the width of the door) but I’m sure we will work something out. They also had some ideas about different door people that might be able to come up with something. We’re going to update our shared spreadsheet with our current picks and see what they recommend.
  • They asked about the battening of the insulation, which is going to be on the external walls of the living quarters. We decided to also add it on the wall between Pete’s office and the hallway. We also discussed better sound deadening plasterboard and better insulation.
  • Lukas mentioned that Lloyd the septic man had visited, but apparently didn’t tell him anything of use. Just told him about his sister’s wedding and made jokes about him not being friends with Ray Jacobs (Lukas said he didn’t have a problem with Ray, just that he wouldn’t call him a good mate).
  • I asked if Penny and Lukas were doing anything for the school holidays - Penny said she was taking the boys to Cattai to her family’s home and I mentioned I was from Cherrybrook and you wouldn’t believe it…they both went to Galston High School!! We are close enough in age we could have played sport together or seen each other at different events, crazy small world! I’ll have to ask if they knew Kim Pike and my other cricket friends, who also went to Galston HS.
  • Lukas also played junior rugby with Stu and his brother Andy - they also now live in Gloucester and Stu is our plumber!
  • Penny also joked about how one time she was on a work call and saw her 14 yr old walking past outside with a cigarette lighter in one hand and propane in the other haha the joys of parenthood!

It was a successful meeting and we are happy with how things are progressing.

Back home at about 3pm I had some lunch and did another hour of work. Then at 4 we headed up for the daily photos. It was much harder to take the third shot today as everything is wider now the carport is coming along, and I can’t stand back far enough because of the perimeter fence hehe

Off for the cow visit - the bubs were mostly hanging around one of the dams and were quick to come over. One of them kept scratching himself on the back of the buggy and I was slightly worried he was going to push us down the hill haha

We might have made a new bread friend, but I don’t think he was too sure.

We thought a bit more about the carport and we think instead of brick columns we might try and do wood beams like we have on the patio areas. And we’re thinking we’ll keep the vertical beam and close in the triangle so it will shelter things a bit more.

ooh good news - a while back we had some concerns that there were no fly screens included in the main quote, but Pete just noticed that our window quote mentions standard fly screens are included, phew!

I had to join a work call at 6pm which was already a bit annoying…then it got changed to 6:15, then 6:45, bah. Luckily it went much better than expected and towards the end I shared something I’d been working on with Scott our DevOps guy, and the CTO said it was exactly what he needed next, yay!

Poor Pete has had a headache all day :( hopefully he’ll be better for the weekend!

Sat 4 Jul

We had our first Skippy visitor! He hung around for a little while. On his second trip across the backyard, I was heading to the toilet and locked eyes with him - I’m not sure who was more surprised haha

I got up at 5am to watch the Socceroos but probably shouldn’t have haha back to bed disappointed at 7am

Did a few checks around the garden. The passionfruit are coming along nicely. Also inspected the new cauliflower a bit more - it will be interesting to see how he goes!

Spent some time trying to work out some bathroom options with AI but it was pretty hit and miss. We were thinking to have this green tile and pattern on the centre shower wall (the wall in the middle of the room) and wondered if we might also use it for the ledge behind the vanity in the adjacent room, but we’re not convinced.

We also debated a bit about tile orientation. Pete was thinking our wall tiles were going to be portrait (600 x 1200) and I was shocked as I thought they would be landscape (1200 x 600) - thankfully AI agreed that mine is the better and more conventional layout. We also wondered whether to align the (600 x 600) square floor tiles with the walls where possible, or was it better to do a diagonal pattern to mix things up? Still a bit on the fence about this one, but I think we’ll probably end up with the regular grid as it should also reduce the amount of edge cuts / wastage. Here’s an example (just of the tile layout, not our actual bathroom).

Headed in to town for the Pokémon Go - Sobble ‘Community Day’ event (it’s funny, the name used to be relevant when we were in the UK and would meet up in big groups, but it’s just Pete and I now!) A bit later we headed out past Kia Ora to the end of the road - you can really see the new house now! Although the better view is slightly back a bit as you can see more between the trees. My photos are hopeless but here they are anyway.

A quick Woolies trip then headed home. I tried to get Pete to take some photos of our new house from the road. He kept trying to take them through the dirty windscreen instead of out the open window haha We also saw a majestic goat up at David’s old place.

A quick cow visit when we got home, but they weren’t too interested in us today. Here is how the house is looking from the top and middle paddocks.

Spent hours more working on bathroom planning and searches, until I became too frustrated and gave up for the night.

Made a second round of Koftas and good thing Pete remembered to have the greek yoghurt with them this time, as I’d forgotten again!

Sun 5 Jul

I startled a hare on one of my early morning toilet visits.

Tried to catch up on some journalling in the morning. The weather was really gloomy - bitter cold and overcast and drizzly, so I was glad to be inside. Later when the sun came out Pete and I headed down to check on the pumpkins. We had decided to pick the last lot so that neighbour Pete could let the cows back in to the lower paddocks. First I spotted some interesting berries1. They looked awesome but we left them alone haha

We picked a batch of pumpkins - some didn’t look quite ripe but we’d see how they went. We left a couple for the cows hehe

Next we headed up to the house site as Pete wanted to measure the rooms to check they were all roughly as planned. The first rooms were as expected but when we got to the kitchen and mudroom they seemed about 5cm out - we measured and re-measured then Pete realised they hadn’t fixed that frame at the top yet hahaha crisis averted.

Pete got up one of the ladders and balanced on a plank (help!) so he could measure the hallway section - this was the problem area that had been affected by the steel beam debacle (which we still didn’t really understand). The initial measurement didn’t seem too bad. A while later we were looking at it again from underneath and I realised there was a huge difference from one end to the other (if you can see the blue panel against the yellow - there’s about an 8cm gap at this end which tapers to about 1cm at the other end). That could be a problem! We thought at first that the frame at the other end could be moved, to straighten things up and give us closer to the original hall width we’d planned - but then we realised the ceiling would have a slight overhang rather than the walls going straight up. So probably we’ll need Lukas to make some extra wall on this side next to the steel beam.

We also noticed something we hadn’t spotted before - it appeared that the sink drainage for the guest ensuite was actually situated in the main bathroom!! As the rooms are adjacent, hopefully it’s not a huge deal but we’ll have to see.

We had a quick visit to see the cows but it was so cold now and overcast again we only stayed a few minutes.

We set the last pumpkin batch out in the kitchen but might move them to the lounge room with the others if we can re-organise things to get a bit of extra space.

I spent the arvo journalling - I’m only a month behind now sigh

Pete has been working on his fancy electical plan.

For dinner Pete made the most delicious roast dinner. While he was finishing the meat, he kept hassling me to try one of his potatoes that was “like a cloud” - he failed to tell me it was a burning hot cloud hahah it was yum though. The meat, carrots and sweet potato were all perfect. The only downside was we’d forgotten to cook the pumpkin! Ah well, next time.

1 - How come every berry I find has to be poisonous haha AI tells me -

“This looks very likely to be Native Bryony / Striped Cucumber — Diplocyclos palmatus.

Do not eat it. Despite the “cucumber” common name, it is treated as poisonous; Australian rainforest plant references note the fruit has been suspected in serious illness and deaths in children, and a bushcare source says all parts are extremely poisonous.

For practical handling: leave it alone or remove it with gloves, especially if kids/dogs might access it.”

entry.title: Build Week 14
entry.content:
Oh no, there’s a new rat poo in the bathroom! I was hoping they’d all died or moved on, boooooo!

A bit of action on site today whith a white Ute and trailer arriving at 6:40, another white Ute and trailer at 6:52 and Lukas in his truck and trailer at 7:19. He left at about 8:20 and returned again at 8:50. Most exciting however, was the arrival at 9:10 of some steal beams!

The truck backed out again at 10:26. Lukas headed off in his truck at 10:41 followed by the two Utes at 10:42 and 10:43.

Had an email from Penny in response to our purchase request, and with an update on the work -

At about 2pm Pete took his drone shot and then we headed up in the buggy. Before I could take a photo of the site, he insisted I take a photo of him on the ‘balance’ beam haha such a pest

Pete wondered why there were different lengths in the beams. I can only hope the engineers know what they’re doing haha

The cows were mostly sitting down when we visited today, so we parked opposite and tried not to disturb them.

There was a funny moment when one of the calves kept following a plover.

We went for a walk around the dam. I think I saw a fish jump! I threw a piece of bread in, but didn’t see any further action.

A quick hello to the cows in neighbour Pete’s paddock, then back to work.

We were going to have nachos for dinner - originally we were going to have them on Sunday night, but we spent too long doing house stuff and it got too late. So we were looking forward to them on Monday, but as we went to make them we realised we hadn’t gotten any mince out of the freezer - worse still, there wasn’t any mince in the freezer haha foiled again We had to settle for freezer pizza and I dropped one of my slices on the floor and half the pineapple fell off, sad.

Tue 23 Jun

The first arrival today was a white Ute and trailer at 6:42, and Lukas with his truck all loaded up a couple of minutes later. Another white Ute and trailer arrived at 6:51.

A man from Bucketts Building Supplies & Services arrived at 9:48 and left about 8 mins later.

But the most exciting arrival was the frames! Pete messaged me from the shower that something was happening, and I could see a truck waiting down on the road. I went out to take a photo and Lukas caught me sticky-beaking on his way down help - he waved and called out hello and said he was a bit worried about getting the truck in - me too!

Pete was out of the shower now so we went to see what was happening - there were 3 men down at the gate but no more truck - we assumed it had gone to turn around somewhere as hopefully it would be easier to drive in from the other direction. We got to the bottom and spoke to Lukas and then we saw the truck coming back. I started to record it but stopped after a bit as I didn’t want to upset the driver. He had to go forward and back a few times to avoid the fences, he did an amazing job!! Lukas and his offsider jumped on the back and rode the truck up to the site.

It didn’t take long for them to unload everything up at the site.

We waited out the back to see the truck leave again - Lukas and his two offsiders rode it down to the bottom so they could help guide him out.

I thought he might have tried to back out the same way he’d driven in, but instead he was driving forwards and trying to turn right, which didn’t appear to be the best angle. He tried a few times but couldn’t make it work, and had to remove one of the fence posts. We headed down to see how things were going and I think Lukas was a bit worried we were going to be upset, but we didn’t mind at all - just glad the truck made it out OK! We can sort the fence once the build is finished.

Now the excitement was over, we headed in to town to get dinner supplies. As I was about to park on the grass at Woolies, the car braked suddenly - it was the Automatic Emergency Braking but we’re not sure what triggered it. It could have been a leek that was in front of us, or the cows in a nearby paddock - or something else entirely that made it think there was an imminent collision. It was actually a bit painful on my chest, but luckily we hadn’t been driving too fast. It did make me a bit concerned about what might happen if it did that in traffic though - someone would probably run up the back of us. And what would happen if it did it at speed? It seemed a bit dangerous. But I guess they’ve done all sorts of tests and the pros outweigh the cons.

Grabbed our groceries, played a little Pokémon, then headed home. Oh we stopped at the memorial park for a few mins and saw the Magpies having a great old game swinging in the tree.

Made some crunchy bread for lunch at about 4pm and updated the journal while we waited for everyone to leave. It’s 4:30 and they’re still here - don’t they know it’s nearly time for my nap! haha

They left at 4:35 and we headed up in the buggy to see how things were looking. Ooh a beam is already up!!

So exciting!!

It was getting late but we just had enough time for a quick cow visit. A few of the bubs came over but then ran away when I tried to give them an orange.

Finally we got our nacho dinner!

Wed 24 Jun

An early, cold and foggy start for whoever arrived at 6:25! The others arrived at 6:34 and 6:51 and it only appeared to be getting foggier.

I had a quick break at 11:15 to water a couple of plants and give the birds seed and water - wow, the frames were going up already!!

Gloucester Valley Landscape Supplies delivered a couple of loads of crusher dust at 12:33 and 1:30.

We saw Lukas and his two offsiders walking down the driveway at about 1:40 so we knew more frames must be arriving soon - we rushed out but the driver was too quick today and was halfway up the driveway before Pete had a chance to get his drone up. We’d have to try and get him on the way out instead.

Lukas invited us up to have a look, so we headed up in the buggy.

Lukas came over for a chat. He asked about the BYD and I said I was still getting used to it. Pete mentioned later that Lukas had asked about the car a few times and maybe we should offer him a test drive. Lukas also mentioned they’d had a bit of panic with one of the beam sizes, as the plans have a wall of storage and some kitchen appliances in a straight row, but the kitchen appliances are 50ml deeper and it wasn’t clear on the plan. He said lucky the beam was too long rather than too short though, and they just had to drill some extra holes in the cement.

Lukas also asked about whether we’d heard from Todd at Viison about the joinery quote, and we said no, we’d actually been discussing that this morning and were probably going to just go with Tod at CDKJ who’d actually bothered to respond to us haha (we didn’t say that last bit to Lukas). Lukas apologised and said he was a bit embarrased that they’d recommended Todd, but we said it was all good and not his fault at all. It’s a shame we couldn’t have gotten another quote for comparison, but given Tod’s quote was fairly in line with the LMD budget (which presumably had been based on previous work with Viison) we hoped things would align.

I think Lukas was a bit sad not to be building the house frames himself, but he mentioned how then he’d have to arrange for an engineer to come and certify them, which sounded like a difficult/time-consuming process. Whereas he said if he gets them pre-fabricated, they already come with a certificate. Seems a bit of a strange process!

We let Lukas get back to work, and sat in the buggy for a few mins while Pete got some drone shots. We headed back to the cottage and I got the bins ready while Pete did some more drone business and got the truck turning around and leaving.

Then we headed into the Post Office as Pete had had a message that there’d been a delivery - we weren’t sure what, but it could be the lights which might be taking up a lot of space, so we didn’t want to leave them too long in case they were in the way. When we arrived, Charlie was out front with the delivery truck, and he came over while Pete went inside - he was interested in the BYD and jumped in, but was not too sure about the seat warmer hahaha we had a good chat and sadly he mentioned that he’d split from his wife 18 months ago. Pete returned and joked about Charlie being in the car saying “he’s a married man!” oh no, bad timing! But it was all fine. We chatted some more about the BYD. Charlie had also mentioned that he was trying to sell his farm out on Barrington East Rd, and that he was currently living in the back of the Post Office (very interesting, I didn’t even realise there was a house attached, how convenient!) He also mentioned his sister and parents lived in town - that was a surprise as I remember his father from when he worked at the Cherrybrook Post Office and I haven’t seen him around town in all the time I’ve been here, I’ll have to keep a better eye out!

Had a little drive around and saw the magpies being silly again. Over near the oval we saw a family of grey-crowned babblers who are my new favourite bird - they were so funny and had interesting chatter and song, and cute little hops.

Back home at 3:45 I had lunch and did a bit more work (great breakthrough on the dictionary key migration, thanks Claude!) while we waited for the builders to leave so we could head up for a look. They keep working late and it’s so cold and getting dark by the time we can go up haha

Can’t believe how much has gone up already!!

Can’t wait until we can have a proper walk around inside!!

Thurs 25 Jun

The usual 3 cars arrived on Thursday - at 6:19, 6:44 and 6:46. One car headed off at 7:28 and came back about twenty minutes later.

A mystery blue car came at 8:19 and left 5 minutes later.

Miserable weather. One car headed off at 8:51 and came back about an hour later - Lukas told us on Friday that he’d taken the team for Breakfast at Roadies cafe. Unfortunately the weather hadn’t improved much but they worked through it.

I wasn’t feeling well, so I just worked in the morning and then took the rest of the day off.

Another white car arrived at 1:07 and left about 30mins later. Not sure who that was. And a black car arrived at 2:50 and left about 40mins later - not sure who that was either, but he at least had his window down when he arrived so I could see his face hehe

Meanwhile Pete and I had spent a little time pottering in the garden. The camellias were flowering more now, and we have a new passionfruit coming! Pete got something on his foot and decided to wash it off in the rainwater bin hehe It looks like the jonquils or daffodils (I can’t remember which!) might be going to flower soon. And we finally got around to planting the new Grevillea!

We saw an email from Penny following up on our EOFY bathroom order -

We started researching some options, but saw the team heading home at about 4:15 so we went up to check out their latest work before it got dark. Overall it didn’t look much different to yesterday, but I think they’d spent a lot of time fastening everything and making it all straight - we could see some string lines set up.

Earlier we’d found one of the tiny watermelons was no longer attached to anything, so we put it in the fridge and now we prepared to cut it. It was only small, but it was yum!

We finished our bathroom research and replied to Penny -

Fri 26 Jun

Rough night and still not feeling great, so I decided to just do another 1/2 day. Slept in a bit, and when I got up I saw there was a big crane up at the house site! Suella had also messaged -

Pete and I thought the crane might be for the windows, but when we went to have a look, they hadn’t arrived yet. The workers were on a break having some organges - I couldn’t see Lukas but there was a new guy in a checked shirt - I was about to say to Pete “I wonder where Lukas is” but then the checked-shirt man came over and it was Lukas in disguise haha He said they hadn’t been able to lift the other beam with the [WHAT’S IT CALLED] so they had to get the crane in - and while they had it, they were making use of it to get more of the roof frame bits up.

The crane was pretty cool, but we hoped it wasn’t blowing out the budget! Here’s a pic of when he arrived at 7:40 -

Had a weird text message from Karissa at Mortgage Choice -

Was that something we had to do or something someone was sending us? Not sure why another valuation was needed.

I watched a bit of the Socceroos v Paraguay match but it was pretty boring and ended 0-0. Awesome that the Aussies will make it through to the next round though!

Later we heard a tractor going up to the house site - it looked like neighbour Pete’s tractor, but when we checked the camera later it wasn’t Pete driving -

We found out later that the crane had gotten bogged and someone had suggested calling neighbour Pete to ask if they could borrow his tractor. Lukas said he didn’t know Pete, but Ribo said he did and gave him a call. Pete walked him through over the phone how to get the tractor working and Ribo then helped get the crane unstuck - it was a young driver and he didn’t know to keep driving once he got unbogged, so it happened more than once I’m led to believe. But how nice of neighbour Pete to come to the rescue!!

As Lukas was leaving for the day, he stopped for a chat with Pete, which was when he heard the story about the crane bogging, but also that a lady had visited earlier from the bank, which was why we got the message from Karissa about the valuation - it’s all part of the standard procedure now that we had submitted a request for the previous stage payment, that they would come out to see if the work was really done / as expected. Lukas also said we could go up to the site and walk around, just don’t bang into anything haha

We headed up and took a couple of snaps, and Pete did a walkthrough.

I saw a white car driving past, which I thought might be Richard and Suella so I waved and then the car tooted back - I messaged them inviting them up to have a look if they wanted and they arrived a few mins later.

We took them on a tour and had a great chat - they were so encouraging and excited for us :)

We also had a rascally visitor from next door. When I first saw him bounding through the paddock I was excited to say hello, but then he jumped all over me and muddied my pants and jumper, boooooo. He was very excited but eventually settled down.

Hopefully he didn’t wee or poo everywhere when we weren’t looking haha

After a good long chat, Richard and Suella headed home, and Pete and I explored a bit more and took some more photos.

The grass has seen better days!

We started walking back to the cottage and I noticed a bottle in the middle of the driveway - I’d forgotten I’d left it there on the walk up, and Richard and Suella must have had to drive over it twice and wonderered what it was doing there haha

The doggo followed us down the driveway, then went to play in the ditch - but then somehow as we were closing the back door behind us, he was following us in! haha sneaky rascal - we had to shoo him out and then when Pete went to the bedroom, he saw him waiting at the front door haha so cute, but no you can’t come in!

Pie and chips for dinner while we watched the end of Berlin on Netflix, and then watched the Roosters in Friday night football.

Sat 27 Jun

Finally caved and made a Waterdrop order - I’ve been wanting to try the Apple flavour for probably more than a year but have never been able to find it in the shops (only Woolies really stocks the brand, but they’ve never had the Apple flavour at any location I’ve checked - and I check every new Woolies I go to haha) The sales were on and it was most economical to get the 5+1 pack, and each pack has 12 cubes, so they better be bloody good or I’ll have a lot of disappointing drinks ahead of me haha

Tried to do a bit of journal before we had some other chores to do. We had been keeping the fire going day and night, but we’d let it go out this morning so we could take out the ash as it was getting too hard to fit the logs in. Pete secured it in the shed so it wouldn’t blow away, and we headed into town. Went to check out bat park but they haven’t progressed any further with the new toilet block, and there were no doggos or new equipment at Gloucester District park, very disappointing hehe

Got some groceries at IGA and Woolies - Pete tried to leave without paying again!!

Got some petrol for the buggy, then headed home. Put the groceries away then went to visit the cows. We’d bought a couple of bananas for them, as we saw a video of a highland cow running over to eat a banana - but our cows weren’t interested. One of the calves did come over to scratch himself on the buggy and give it a bit of a lick haha

We saw little Wonkleg on the other side of the fence so went to see if he was OK. Although he was on his own, it looked like the other bubs were looking out for him, so that’s good.

We drove back around and stopped on the hill watching the cows for a bit longer. Pete was freezing to death in his shirt and shorts but he didn’t tell me until we were leaving!

Next we headed to the house site to take another look around and discuss a few different things. We spotted ‘Support Here’ on one of the beams which we thought was interesting hehe

Headed home for a late ‘lunch’ snack (it was some time between 4:30-5pm!) and spent the next few hours looking for more sale items for the bathrooms - I think we settled on some mixers, spouts, shower heads and mirrors for the main bathroom and two ensuites. All added to the shared spreadsheet so hopefully Penny could purchase them on Monday before the EOFY sales end.

Sun 28 Jun

Well it turns out we hadn’t settled on the bathroom items as Pete found more overnight and had sent me a few links - I had a look while he had his shower but nothing was jumping out to me. We’d look again after our errands.

We were up early to head to Woolies to try and grab a Vienna loaf before they sold out - I had to dodge a trolley and dash past another lady but I managed to get the last one hehe we picked up the other supplies we needed so Pete could attempt to make a replica City Edge sandwich like we used to get in Surry Hills.

After Woolies we headed to the memorial park so we could feed the Magpies some peanuts. Then out to the industrial area to see if there were any pallets - we were in luck! We are going to try and grow the strawberries in one, vertically.

Next on the agenda was a Happy Birthday video message for Andy - I’d been putting it off as I wasn’t really sure what to do or say, but in the end I only did 1 take and I think it turned out OK.

Then we buggied over to see the cows, but we were only there a moment when we spotted an egret that looked injured, near the dam. We went closer to investigate and it was clear he had a busted wing. Pete was able to pick him up and I drove us back to the shed, and we put the bird in a box and Pete called Fawna. Unfortunately they said there wasn’t anything they could do, so our options were either -

  • Pete could try to put it out of its misery
  • We could leave it in the box overnight and take it to the vet in the morning to be euthanised
  • We could take it back to the dam where it would probably get eaten by a fox or something overnight

We didn’t really know what to do and debated what would be the best option for the poor thing - I thought I could at least give him a nice meal of things from the garden, but it turns out he’s a strict carnivore so I couldn’t even cheer him up with a snack. I got a bit teary, but in the end we decided the most ‘natural’ thing was to take him back to the dam. So we buggied back out there and put him in a little hollow. Poor bugger. I hope he doesn’t suffer too much more.

Drove back home so I could wash my hands, then we headed down to check on the pumpkins - quite a few were looking ripe so we gave them the chop.

Then we drove up to the house site so Pete could get some measurements for his cable basket. He’s trying to work out how to get all the cables from the server room through the ceiling to the other parts of the house.

I walked home while he tried to do a PolyCam of the inside of the house structure but it didn’t turn out too well.

We’ll try again once the walls are up and it should work better - it will be a 3D render that we can also pick points and it will show us correct measurements, which will be handy.

The next few hours were spent reviewing bathroom options again as Pete was quite keen on the new brushed bronze items he’d found. We got frustrated with each other because I feel like Pete doesn’t care about the budget, and he thinks I only care about how much things cost and just pick the cheap thing instead of what I actually like or what looks good. He wishes I would just pick what I like first, before looking at the price, but I don’t want to get attached to something we can’t afford. He says there’s no point spending $1.6 million on a house if it turns into a ‘K-Mart’ house because we penny-pinch on all the interior - but I think it’s crazy that we’re already forecasting more than $1.6 million on this house and still struggling to stay within the fixture quotes. Anyway we did a lot of different image renders with AI trying to compare what we’d originally picked (black fixtures) with the bronze ones and in the end we decided we both did prefer the black ones.

Next we looked at toilet roll holders - rivetting stuff. Then a short look at towel racks which will no doubt be a future debate as I’m not sure we need $800 vertical heated racks in every bathroom, but we’ve put that decision off for another time.

It got late and we were both mentally exhausted, so we decided to postpone our big City Edge dinner, as it was going to involve crumbing schnitzel and cooking potato salad, and we also had a heap of washing up to get through first. I think we’ll just have enough energy for the wash-ups hehe oh and we have some washing to hang as well, bugger. Off I go then…

…well we’d hung 90% of the washing and then I found a mouse in one of Pete’s shirts, yay! Back in the wash it all goes. Now it’s 9:30, we’ve just finished the washing up, the washing isn’t going to be ready for another 90+ minutes, and we still haven’t made dinner sigh

entry.title: Build Week 13
entry.content:
Monday I was up at 8:45 to start getting ready for our trip to Newcastle. We headed off at about 10:40. Our first stop was to drop the floor sample back at Choices Flooring.

Whenever we’re at home, Pete is always thinking of things we need to do in Taree or Newcastle, but whenever we actually go, he never wants to go anywhere. Today was the same - even though we’d made a list the day before - he didn’t want to go to any of those places anymore. Oh well. So I decided to go to Charlestown Westfield.

It was hard getting around the tight carpark turns in the Shark, but I managed it. Parked waaaay up the back haha

First stop was Just Cuts to finally get my hair cut (it had been 9 months I think since my last one, eep!)

We had a look around Big W but it was a bit gruelling due to a screaming kid haha

Tried to get a Boost but it wasn’t where we thought it was haha Up, down, and back up the escalator we went - I hope no-one was watching us, they would have thought we were mad haha

Went to the Lego store and Pete excitedly pointed out a new Tintin Moon Rocket lego -

It was pretty cool, but it reminded me that we already have some awesome Tintin figurines of the same theme, that we got in Belgium that must be in storage somewhere - it will be like Christmas when we eventually go through all our boxes again once the new house is built!

T2 next as I had a voucher to use. I contemplated the Strawberries & Cream tea (which sounded horrible, but they had some there to taste and it was quite nice) but I settled on Pumping Pomegranate. It was free because of the voucher, and for some reason I got to choose another free tea as well! I picked ‘Sleep Tight’ - “A trio of lemon balm, lavender and rose to help you wind down at sundown.”

Finally found Boost - it’s always a great treat when we come to the city hehe

Headed to Myer next - it was my biannual underwear purchasing time as I only ever buy during the mid-year or Boxing Day sales hehe

Just as we were leaving Myer, Pete had a missed call from ‘Joe’ from the Doors place - he called them back and when a lady answered, he asked for Joe…turns out it was ‘Jo’ and that’s who we were speaking to hehe she wanted to follow up on a quote we’d requested and had a few questions for us.

Pete ordered some donuts for the Gerros fam while I went to Woolies. Still can’t find Apple Waterdrop, but I was able to get the ‘Extra Perk’ (free) pastry that wasn’t available in our local Woolies, yay! Also bought Pete some lolly teeth from a treat shop nearby.

We were done at Westfield and Pete still didn’t want to go anywhere else, so we just headed over to Gerros.

Issy was the greatest and let us borrow her room for the night ♥︎

We all had a little catch up, then Pete finally decided where he wanted to visit - Cetnaj for a quote on some electrical bits. There was a bit of a debate about who would drive - I had such a good parking spot I didn’t want to lose before the big meter box delivery tomorrow, so Liam very kindly drove us. Pete spent some time explaining what he needed to the sales guys - it was all double Dutch to me, so I watched a little World Cup on the TV nearby. Then we all headed to Coles for some snacks.

Later back at the Gerros residence, Pete was helping the family with some tech jobs so I sat out of the way in the lounge room for a bit. Bill gave me a book he’d finished - Jackdaws by Ken Follett - and I started reading it. Vicki brought me a fluffy blanket when she found out I was cold, so sweet!

Beef stroganoff for dinner - but it was cheesy and there weren’t too many mushrooms, yay! hehe I was super hungry and realised I’d only eaten 1 1/2 cinnamon donuts all day!

We got an update on Vicki’s health - she’ll have to have an operation on her thyroid before Christmas - the docs weren’t sure exactly when as there’s a waiting list and it will also depend on what happens after her next heart tests.

Pete and I spent some time in the lounge room as the fire was on and it was lovely and warm. But I felt bad that Vicki was all alone in the living room (the lounge room was too hot for her!) so we went in there for a bit and chatted and watched a show.

Later we sat in the bedroom and Vincheddar played with us.

I didn’t sleep very well due to the unusual surroundings and the kitty who napped with us (I kept worrying I was going to squish her!) - though the bed was very comfortable and warm! I was a bit stressed about the pending delivery and also had bad cramps, no fun.

The delivery driver arrived with the meter boxes just before 10 - we jumped out of bed and quickly put warmer clothes and shoes on and headed out to meet him. I drove the Shark to the other side of the road and backed up to the tail lift so the guys could just move the items across. Liam is always so helpful in situations like this! He jumped up to help lift things and then dashed to move the Delica so I could re-park in the most ideal spot, and then helped Pete secure everything in the back.

There wasn’t much I could do to help so I went to have my shower. Then I had a look at the plants Vicki had generously gotten for us at the Tocal Field Days - Red Gums, Tallowwood and a Lemon Myrtle ♥︎ She’s looking after them for us until after Winter.

Had more chats and Pete tried to help with more TV and technical things. Then we got packed and ready to go. They’d done a great job securing the meter boxes.

We headed off - to the lock place first. We were a bit confused as they weren’t where we remembered them, but it turns out they’d moved / been bought. Pete gave them some information so they could look up an old order for us - they said they’d get back to us with the part numbers we were after.

Pete didn’t have any further requests, so we just headed to the schnitty sandwich place then got on our way home. At Williamtown we saw some jets taking off!!

Then we visited the pet produce shop - we’d always wanted to drop in but they’d always been closed at the times we were going past.

We bought some bird seed and headed on our way again.

Next stop Stroud to look in Crafty Friends, the homemade and antique gift shop. Pete quite liked the cow bell, but we decided to think about it. I found an awesome duck that you could wind up and he’d whizz along with his head propellers spinning haha so cool - I couldn’t see a price and debated what my limit would be, while the saleslady tried to find out (she had to call someone!) We eventually found that there was a box hiding on another shelf - the $28 price was a bit more than my limit, but it was worth a bit more now it had a box, and also while I was waiting I’d googled similar products online and they were going for $25-$50 so I decided to treat myself.

We got home at 3:50 and with the help of Pete’s fancy dolly (and muscles) we were able to unload the meter boxes OK.

We were happy to be home in time to see the cows.

We saw someone had visited and left tracks - we’d have to check the cameras!

Finally got to eat my schnitty lunch hehe

Later we had an email from Penny -

We got around to checking the cameras, and it was Hunter Pods who’d visited us at 12:26 for 10 minutes. We weren’t sure if they picked up the leftover insulation or maybe brought more insulation for the frames - we’d have to check tomorrow.

Back to work on Wednesday, boooooo.

Had a call from BYD about an administrative error - apparently our car had been sold to us as a 2026 build when in fact it was a 2025 build. They were offering us a refund of $1,100 (the dealer delivery fee) and said we’d be sent more information soon. We’d have to check our insurance wasn’t affected. I did a quick search online and thought we might be entitled to more than $1,100 due to loss of resale value, but we’d have to see.

Heard from Mum that Dad was able to swap the light drivers for us, that was good news (thanks Dad!)

When we did our daily site visit, we saw that the remaining white insulation bits had been collected.

We had a nice cow visit. One of the mums was happily munching away while we sat in the buggy. A couple of the bubs were testing their strength against each other hehe

Corned beef lunch and back to work.

Nothing through from BYD yet.

Meanwhile a crow thieved one of our oranges. At least he ate some though, rather than just chopping it and leaving it!

Pete fixed the washing machine now the new part had arrived - but oh no, we accidentally overflowed the sink because it was blocked with a container haha

I started watching State of Origin while Pete spent some time checking through the new meter boxes to make sure everything was as expected.

The Pest man arrived on Thurs at 10:06 and left 3 hours later.

Pete and I drove in to town around 2:30 - the bloody screens went off at the corner again!

Parked at Woolies and headed to the door - we overheard a couple commenting on the Shark and we mentioned it was ours and we ended up having a long chat and giving them a closer look inside. They were interesting characters. They’re from Rookhurst and their son is considering buying a Shark so they were quite interested to hear what we thought of it so far.

We got home at around 3:40 and headed up to the house site. We could see the pest man had installed what I assume is the termite protection that Penny had referred to.

On the buggy trip up, Pete had flown his drone while I drove, and then he landed it on top - he was very proud of his achievement haha

On to see the cows, they’re so cute! One of them kept mooing really loud and deep haha

Got my mammogram results - all clear, woohoo!

On Friday we had a heap of strange emails from all the suppliers of the appliances we’d ordered -

We’d paid the deposit to Winnings a week ago so were hoping all was in order and it was just some weird automation in their systems.

At 1:40 we buggied down to cut some lemons and then drove into town to the share shop and swapped them for some chokos.

Went to Woolies and then had a sticky-beak at the new grocer on the main street. Their produce looks pretty nice.

Back home just before 3 and headed on a cow visit.

The BYD refund link finally arrived but we didn’t do anything about it yet - we were worried that taking that money might prevent us from seeking further compensation, if we decided to.

We got the quote back from Jo for the doors - 12 pages and a whopping $47K, what the hell! Pete realised they’d included the main glass doors from the dining area to the patio, which were already covered by the builder, so we asked for those to be removed and hoped it would bring the costs down!!

Debated whether to watch the World Cup at 5am…watched some of the first half - the Aussies scored, but unfortunately for the other team haha it was 2-0 at half time and I went back to bed. I dreamed Australia won 9-3 hahaha When I got up again I skipped through the second half but there were no more goals, sad.

I’d recently been contacted by Bec, a lady I used to know from my Deepend days as she was the partner of Andy who I used to work with.

What a fantastic idea! I spent most of the day preparing a note and searching through old pictures.

Pete and I went into town for Pokémon Community Day (Frigibax this time). When we got home we went to see the cows and play them some music.

In other news, it looks like a plover might be nesting on the little island in one of the dams.

And someone must have dinged the house site fence!!

Went for my Sunday morning walk up to the house site - I wonder what I’ll do when we live at the new house…walk down to the old one instead I guess hehe

Around 1pm we headed down in the buggy to check on the pumpkins. The vine was starting to die down now. Neighbour Pete’s cows were wondering what we were up to hehe

Next we went to visit the cows on our block. The white bub was making all sorts of silly shapes trying to scratch itself on the bank haha

A couple of the cows came over for a good scratch on the buggy.

Headed over to check on the natives - they were looking good. On the way back we thought we saw a water bottle in the distance, but as we got closer we realised it was a huge mushroom!

Did some grass chops when I got back to the cottage - finally finished what Dad started around the tank hehe

2pm had lunch and started looking for lights and vanities. 4:30 still going. 5:30 still going, and hating life - the sink we picked was out of stock, and delivery fees were insane (like $500!!)

Feels like we have a never-ending list of things to pick and things that aren’t included in the original quote.

We emailed Penny with a few of our first selections for vanities and toilets.

Then we purchased some lights for the dining and lounge spaces (as these were outside the quote).

A bit of progress made but still a lot more research to do and decisions to make!

entry.title: Build Week 12
entry.content:
Public holiday, woohoo!

I spent some time ordering all the chores I needed to do today and this week. I wish I could just sit in the sun and read a book haha the sun isn’t out today though :(

I had to keep fixing Looby, who was having a hell of a time in the slightly longer grass out the front. Instead of his usual methodical lines, he’d been zagging all over the place like he was possessed haha

I tried to catch up on some journal…I finished the first pass of Week 10 and tried to finish Week 8 with some bits I’d been waiting on from Pete.

We put some washing on, but it errored twice - the second time we looked up on the computer what the error meant and were informed “water not filling up in time”. We went out to the laundry to have another look and saw water on the floor. Pete moved the washing maching into the mudroom and lay it on its side - a bloody rat had chewed through one of the pipes!!

It looks like we can get a new bit of pipe for $33 from Perth. But what to do about the wet unwashed clothes - ask the neighbours if we can do a load at their place? Pete preferred to try the laundromat in town. He spent bloody ages tying everything up in the tray of the Ute and dirtied/wet an (old) doona, when I thought we could have just put the washing in a couple of garbage bags on the floor in the back of the car - but he gets in these moods sometimes where he thinks he knows best and it’s not up for discussion!!

We drove into town and parked across from the laundromat. All the inside walls were covered in different signs and we didn’t know where to look first. We finally found the prices and I wished I hadn’t hahaha

I put $20 in the machine to get coins back and Pete went out to get the laundry and then he put it in the big machine. He didn’t think it would fit in the small machine, but I thought it was worth trying to save $10 - so I moved everything over when he went to get the detergent from the car hehe plenty of room!!

I put the money in but nothing happened - it better not have eaten my coins! Nope I just hadn’t secured the door properly hehe

The wash would take 25mins. There was a penalty if you didn’t collect your washing soon enough, but it didn’t seem like the place was busy (only saw an older guy taking his stuff out) so hopefully we wouldn’t have to rush back.

Headed to Woolies first to get some bread rolls for dinner. Then Pete wanted to go see the goats but I had something else in mind - I’d downloaded a geocaching app and the recommended first ‘easy’ location nearby was at the old St Clements Historic Park. The description said “In the grounds of the old St Clements church and grave yard. There is now an old school building (locked) with period desks and some other historical items scattered around the locality. The cache is a small, easy find not suitable for trackables.” We didn’t really know what we were looking for but had a hunt around the site. We weren’t having much luck so I looked at past finders and saw a photo, so we were able to work out the rough location to check more thoroughly. I looked in an old bit of metal but didn’t look well enough - Pete had another look and found the container.

It was spidery so I let him retrieve it hehe He handed it to me and I went to lean on the pole nearby and got a shock when the container rapidly attached itself haha it had a strong magnet inside, which was how it had been secured to its hiding spot.

We couldn’t decide who would take a photo so we both did hehe We had a look inside and wrote our names in the log. We didn’t read the other bit of paper as it was too wet.

We headed to quickly see the goats.

We retrieved our washing and headed home, hoping to have time for a quick cow visit before it got dark. We were glad we did as the young ones were really friendly again, one in particular had a good sniff and lick of the back of the buggy haha

Wonkleg was still limping but at least he was around all his young friends and had Mum nearby.

Back home we hung the washing in front of the fire and then finally posted Week 8 of the journal (only 3 weeks late haha)

I kept wondering why I smelled corn chips and realised Pete had camouflaged one on the yellow belly of my frog coaster hahaha

Pete emailed Penny -

No site visitors today.

Willie was having a great time riding Looby hehe

We headed in to town at about 1:30 - the car was looking nice and shiny!

I was getting a bit sick of the road work on The Bucketts haha but it will be great when it’s all finished.

The whole reason for today’s trip into town was because Pete had said we had an important delivery at the Post Office - it turns out it was just the TradeMutt shirts he’d ordered, which were clearly not urgent at all - he’s such a pest!!

On the plus side, we got to see some beautiful camellias in the park.

We got home at about 2:30 and went on our daily cow visit.

Captain Willie was still having the time of his life, and Pete gave him an appropriate soundtrack.

It was a looooong day as I did 3 shifts and ended up working 10.5 hours. But it will be worth it as I can work less on Friday when Mum and Dad visit 😁

Wednesday was time for pour #2!

Lukas arrived at 6:49, a white car at 6:54, a white Ute and trailer at 7:02, another white Ute at 7:15 and the pump truck from Pacific Coast Pumping at 7:33.

I had in my notes for the day ‘angry face on white box’ and I can’t remember now (30 days later) what I was referring to, but it could have been this white box on the pump truck (in hindsight I think it looks like a robot rather than an angry face hehe)

The first cement truck arrived at 8:27, backing straight up to the house site.

At 8:43 I could see two trucks waiting out on the road - I wondered if Lukas had asked them not to wait on the grass this time?

Cement truck 1 came back down and parked in front of the shed - cement truck 2 headed up to the house site at 8:45 and truck 1 cleaned and left at 8:50. Cement truck 3 then came and waited in front of the shed at 8:53.

At 9am, trucks 2 and 3 swapped. (Side note - the driver of truck 3 must be driven crazy by the sound his truck makes haha)

Truck 4 arrived at 9:06 and waited in front of the shed. Truck 2 has cleaned and leaves at 9:12.

At 9:15, trucks 3 and 4 swapped.

Truck 3 cleans and leaves at 9:18. Truck 4 doesn’t leave until quite a while later at 9:45.

Truck 5 arrives at 10:53 and doesn’t leave until 11:30.

The pump truck leaves at 12:05.

It was a quicker and smoother pour than the first one (but a smaller area as well).

At 12:49 Pete and I headed up to the house site and had a chat with Lukas - he apologised for the recent delays but we said we weren’t too worried. He also said he’d chased Todd for us regarding the kitchen joinery quote.

We went for a cow visit, but they weren’t as excited to see us today, sad.

Lukas left at 1:05. I got back to work. The white Ute left at 1:33, then came back at 2:15 and left again at 3:18.

Meanwhile there’d been some big news in the community regarding the bakery.

The charges against the individual were amounting to $13,000 in penalties and against the company it was a whopping $70,000 plus nearly $10K in professional costs.

It was all quite controversial and divisive within the local community, with some people saying the place was gross and they’d never go there, and others saying the accusations were from years ago and irrelevant.

Back to the house site. The white car left at 3:27. Pete did his drone shot. The white Ute left at 3:28 with some rio.

Just after 3:30 we headed on another site visit - aww how cute are we haha

We wrote our initials near our bedroom.

Back to work again. But Pete made me cheesy hammy toast, yay! ♥︎

We’d received a few emails throughout the day, including from Penny and Keryn.

Pete had also contacted Fair Trading about the Shelly items.

No visitors on Thursday morning.

I noticed on the cameras that Pete cleaned some of the bird poop off the Shark, what a guy!

My belly was really upset ahead of my Mammogram. We left at about 1:15 and luckily weren’t held up by the roadworks. I parked at the park and walked over to the bus. I saw Kym go in and thought she must have the appoinment before me, but she just had a quick chat to the ladies and then left, wishing me well on her way past. The 1:30 appointment hadn’t turned up so I (1:40) got to go a little early, yay! Both the ladies were lovely as usual. I’d forgotten to bring a hair tie again, d’oh! But luckily they always have some spare. It was all over pretty quick and didn’t hurt as much as last year, yay!

We headed to the car wash next - in hindsight I should have dropped Pete there as he did most of the work and would have been mostly finished while I was at my appointment. I tried to assist with the ‘high pressure’ wash but didn’t realise until halfway through that there was a trigger I was supposed to be pulling, so it had been more like a delicate spray, oops, what a dope! Luckily Pete knew what he was doing hehe

Over to Woolies next to get some supplies for the weekend.

Back home we visited the house site and then said hello to the cows at the fence.

We got confirmation from Bing Lee that the refund was being processed - what a relief to finally have that over with!

Woke up on Friday excited for Mum and Dad’s visit! I worked 3hrs in the morning until their arrival at 11:45. Pete and I expertly guided them in haha

Hug time! Dad got one too but he was hiding behind the boot, so no pics for him hehe

I excitedly pointed out the Red Train! It had taken me weeks to see it, and they fluked it in the first few minutes! haha Next we spent some time unloading the lights Dad had collected for us from Cosmo in Castle Hill.

We had a chat and ate the Cambodian snacks Mum and Dad had brought us from the food stall in Ward’s River. They’d also brought us a heap of treats from Hattam farm - eggs, honey, cheese, beetroot relish and some fancy salt. And Dad had made some Anzac biscuits! So spoiled we were!! We ate lunch while watching some of the Korea v Czechia World Cup match.

Pete had been examining all the new lights, and it looked like some of them had the wrong LED driver - we’d have to send them back to get swapped.

After lunch we headed off in the buggy to check out the house site - as we left I was a bit worried Looby was heading for the Jag, but it was a false alarm hehe

We had a look around and explained where the different rooms were. I demonstrated where our bed would be hehe

Next we went to visit the cows, but they weren’t too interested in us or Dad’s bread offering hehe

What a view!

We took Mum and Dad to see the new rocky site we’d recently discovered. Meanwhile, how good are all the neighbour’s trees looking! Hopefully ours will be doing that well in another year or so too!

Next we headed to check out our planting site. Dad was opening the gate for us when suddenly he jumped back clutching his arm. The others weren’t too sure what had happened but I soon realised he’d zapped himself! The gate shouldn’t have been electrified, we’d have to investigate. Poor Dad :(

We had a look around. The poor peach tree didn’t have any leaves left but hopefully it would come good again in Spring. Most of the other plants were looking pretty good. Dad did a re-enactment of his shock for my journal hehe then he went exploring and very nearly got himself again! I had the camera ready that time just in case hehe

Dad stepped on the poor plant that Pete had previously stepped on a number of times - poor bugger isn’t having a good run but hopefully he’ll pull through haha

We found out the fence had been burning our tape, though this wasn’t the reason the fence was electrified.

We buggied back to the Cottage and had a look around the garden. It was nice to see the Lady O Grevillea flowering. We were also pleased with how the passionfruit was going. Pete snuck in a hug hehe

Mum and Dad headed to the motel to check in at about 2:45 and I got back to work for another couple of hours.

Pete and I paid the Winnings appliances deposit - help! We hadn’t been paying attention and they required 30% not 10% as we’d initially expected. It was fine, we just had to shuffle some money around.

When Mum and Dad returned, we headed up to see the cows and the sunset. We saw the birds on their nightly flyover as well.

I made a cabbage salad and Pete cooked his marinated pork for dinner.

Dad went exploring but couldn’t see any owls or rabbits.

We watched the Roosters in a disappointing loss to the Dolphins, 48-10. On the plus side, two of our young guys on debut (Bassingthwaighte and Rodwell) both scored.

We had an entertaining few minutes when Mum and Dad were trying to leave and Dad couldn’t remember how to turn the Jag’s lights on - ah it’s no good getting old is it!

A nice sunny morning on Saturday. Mum and Dad arrived around 10 and we had a chat. Then we headed out to do some work in the garden. Mum modelled her fancy sunnies for me :)

Dad started chopping the grass over near the caravan while Mum helped him tidy - I was hoping they didn’t run into any snakes! Meanwhile I trimmed and restaked the tomatoes and tidied grass out of the garden beds while Pete the slacker was still napping hehe

It was already looking much improved so we treated ourselves to a drinks break and a chat. It was a lovely day and it was nice to relax under the tree.

When Dad got to chopping again, he accidentally punctured an old milk bottle that was hidden in the long grass. We didn’t know what “wettable sulphur” was, or more importantly, if what was in the bottle was even what was on the label! So we gloved up, put some dirt on it and dug out that area and put it in a couple of garbage bags - an expert disposal team we were hehehe

It was after midday now and Pete was awake and having his shower. We had some Cambodian leftovers for lunch along with Jatz with beetroot relish and the special Brie - delicious! Pete wasn’t adventurous and just had Jatz hehe

We were having a nice time relaxing under the tree when oh no - a bird pooped on me!! How bloody rude! haha

After lunch we were contemplating a drive out Skibo way to show Mum and Dad the scenery. We had been a bit unsure if Mum would be able to get into the Shark, as it was so high up, but with the little step we’d bought from Bunnings it was no trouble, yay!!

We drove out to the tiny home, enjoying the cows and scenery on the way. Mum got out of the Shark too quick and didn’t use the step!! But luckily she didn’t injure anything. We’d be more careful in future!

Everyone liked the views. One day we’d like to climb up the hill - we wondered if we could ask permission from the owner, if we could find out who they were.

Next we drove out to see the view of our house from the end of Kia Ora road. Then back into town to admire the falling camellias in the park. On the way home we stopped at the medical centre carpark, so I could demonstrate how difficult it was to park the Shark. I want to be able to nose into a spot in 1 go and it just seems impossible, even with all the cameras.

I thought we were going to have a rest when we got home, but Mum and Dad were straight back to work! haha

After a little while, we took the buggy down to see the pumpkins. Dad found a new big one that was even better than the last one, yay!

Also found this, whatever it is! Claude thinks it might be an Earthball fungus - like everything interesting we seem to find in the garden, it’s toxic haha

We buggied back up past the house and I tried to get a photo of us all waving but there was much confusion and people looking in different directions - we’d try again later!

We went to visit the cows. It was quite cute how they were playing in the trees.

They moved on after a little while and Dad got out for a walk. I was a bit worried a cow might run at him hehe Pete got out as well and Mum and I waited in the buggy. Then Pete came back and drove us over to the fence. The cows were down in the hollow now.

Pete did some work on the dodgy fence, wrapping up some of the wire that had gotten all jumbled - the cows had been freely walking through that section now, so we tidied it up and now we had a gap we could drive through too. We headed back that way and over to the central gate - as we were driving up we wondered what time the birds had flown over yesterday and if they would be coming again today - well we were right on time as here they came!

Back home we did another camera drive-by but were still hopeless - we’d try again tomorrow!

We’d been considering going to the Golf Club for dinner, but in the end decided on Thai take-away. Pete, Dad and I headed in to town and ordered Thai style fried rice with prawns (Mum), two Panang curries (me + Pete), yellow curry with beef (Dad), Thai beef salad (Pete), and two large steamed rice.
