While we were waiting for the order to be made, we drove over to the Bat park to see what they were doing (new toilet block?) but it didn’t look like they’d made much progress and it was a bit dark to see much.

We went to pick up the dinner but when we arrived there was some urgent whispering and it sounded like they’d forgotten to make one of our meals haha but luckily it didn’t take much longer.

Got home and found Mum had rinsed all the washing up for us, how nice!

We watched a ‘feel good’ movie while we ate, but it was a bit misleading as it was a bit sad really!!

We did some quizzes together then Mum and Dad headed home. They saw a bandicoot on the way, how cool!

Pete did some sneaky wash-ups while I was asleep!

Around 4:30 I was up for a wee and none of the bloody lights would come on haha

Mum and Dad arrived at about 10am on Sunday and we did some more work outside - I continued weeding the garden beds and Mum and Dad continued tidying in front of the caravan.

There was some debate about what to do with the junky bits. Later when Pete was out of the shower we asked his advice - shall we move some bits to between the caravan and the white shed? I realised we could take stuff to the tip now we had the Shark. I thought Pete agreed it would be a good idea to take the old sheet metal to the tip, but then later he was annoyed I’d gotten him all sweaty and was asking too much before he’d woken up, d’oh! (Later when Pete was reading the journal he informed me that he was only teasing and not really annoyed, but that’s not how I remember things! hehe)

We put some old rags down in the Shark tray and carefully carried all the jaggy, rusty old bits over. Pete secured everything with more rags and masking tape and straps, and we headed on our way.

We got to the tip and got weighed on the way in. We were pleased to see that it was free to dispose of scrap metal, woohoo!

We drove to the correct section of the tip but there were two scavengers in the way. They took their time but eventually moved on. We parked and started unloading. I was going to help but then I saw a spider so I got out of the way again haha

We secured the rags and straps and headed off, getting weighed again on the way out.

We drove into Barrington - first we had a look at some houses then went to find some cows - some came to the fence to greet us.

Pete wanted some hot chippies so we stopped at the Servo. They turned out pretty well, nice and crispy and chicken salty. Mum and I also shared a Splice drink, yummo!

We drove to Relfs Landing for a different view and to eat some more chippies. Mags came to visit and we shared a couple with his family.

Next we went to have a look at the house being built on Dangar Rd (they’ve got windows now, yay!) then to the second-hand bookshop (didn’t buy anything) then to IGA to buy the gravy Bill had requested.

As we were heading back down Bundook Rd, a cop flew up behind us and sped past - not something we see much in this area, I wonder where they were headed!

We continued out towards Bundook to try and see where we were yesterday when we were out Skibo way. We drove through a tunnel (a very tight squeeze!) on a side road, to see the (locked) gate for the road we think joins back up to where we were at the tiny house.

Got back home and saw the Socceroos match against Turkey was 0-0 after 20mins. We settled down to watch and didn’t have to wait long before GOAAAAAL to Irankunda, what a beauty! We had some leftovers for lunch, pleasantly surprised at how well Australia were playing. Then GOAAAAAL to Metcalfe in the 75th minute - could we actually win this? WOW yes we could!! A bit of an upset to beat Turkey 2-0 - what a great start for our World Cup!

After the football we did some more work out in the garden. The area in front of the caravan was looking SO much better - thanks Mum and Dad!! ♥︎

Dad still couldn’t rest for the day, and started chopping the grass around the tank.

Pete picked an orange for us to try - it was delicious!

We thought about planting the Grevillea but we’d run out of time. We’d only just be able to fit in a quick site and cow visit before it started to get dark.

We’d mastered our buggy-wave now, getting great shots from 3 different angles today haha Pete even got 2 hands going at one point (he was supposed to be driving!) what a show-off haha

Up at the house site we had a wander through the rooms again and Dad tried out the guest bedroom hehe

The sun had gone down but we just had time for a quick cow visit. Most of the bubs were with their Mums having a drink, but one of the bubs was interested to see us.

It was mostly calm among the herd, except for two little rascals who were carrying on hehe

We headed home and had a little sit before starting dinner. I tried the corned beef in the air fryer in four pieces this time, so we all got our own crispy end bits - it turned out really well!

Another great visit and memories made ♥︎

entry.title: Build Week 11
entry.content:
When we checked the cameras on Monday, we saw that BunBun had visited a couple of times last night -

A white Hyundai and a white Isuzu ute went up to the house site just after 7.

Some good bird action on the cameras this morning!

After my shower, I had a look around the garden. Unfortunately it’s looking like half the snapdragons are already dying :( hopefully the other ones will survive! Inside, the coriander and parsley were looking sick too.

In other sad garden news - I saw Willie eat a butterfly!!

Pete was up early as he wasn’t feeling well :(

Knobby were having an EOFY sale so I bought 7 pairs of undies for Pete so we could qualify for the free bag as well.

The ute left at 11:55 but was back 20 mins later.

Joni sent me some feedback from her trip to Norfolk Island, which was nice and helpful.

The ute left at 12:44 and the Hyundai at 12:46.

Around 2:30 we headed up to see the new cows. We saw one little one all alone on the bank, he didn’t get up to go with the others.

There were lots of bubs - a couple were so cute and tiny!

Everyone seemed a bit wary of us, which I guess was understandable.

Next we headed over to see the natives. They were mostly good, but the peach was looking a bit sick.

Neighbour Pete pulled up just as we were leaving, and we had a good long chat. It was a lovely sunny day. Sadly another of his cows had recently died, a young one this time. He talked about how he’d swapped our cows over and how the new group had a little one with a sore leg. He also offered that his mate Clarkey, who’s staying in his cottage, could probably mow in between our natives one day when he had a free afternoon. That would be great as it was already getting quite overgrown with grass and weeds!

We buggied back and saw that the little bub was still sitting alone on the hill - he was probably the one with the wonky leg. We saw his Mum go and check on him so hopefully all would be well.

Stopped at the house site and saw that more of the formwork had been done.

Pete was in a hurry to get back for the Trademutt sale - hopefully he didn’t splurge too much hehe

We had a nice sunrise on Tuesday morning.

The bloody Peewee harassed me all morning - constantly flying at my office window, it’s covered in poopy footprints. Here are some examples of his mischief.

I messaged the fridge man as he hadn’t contacted us on Sunday like he said he would.

The concreter (maybe?) came at 1:18 and left only about 4 mins later - I was at my desk and didn’t even notice! But Pete heard a vehicle while he was in the shower and we saw it later when checking the cameras.

It was a lovely sunny day - 20 degrees! It was only 11 degrees in the mudroom so I opened all the windows up.

At about 1:40, Pete and I headed down to the orchard in the buggy - I got to try out my new long clippers to try and get some lemons for the Share Shop. The clippers were great but it was still harder than I thought it would be, trying to get high enough and the right angle. I struggled with one tree getting just a few, then realised there was another tree that was loaded so got those instead hehe Pete complained I kept chopping them with the thorns still on haha

Went to visit the cows - they were near the centre gate, on both sides of the middle fence. We sat on the other side of the fence for a bit, not wanting to disturb them. Then we decided we should check if little wonk leg was OK. We started to drive towards where we’d last seen him on the bank over the back of the farm. We noticed one of the Mums was on her own on the other side of the hill to the rest of thte herd, and she was watching us and looking over towards where we’d last seen the bub. As we drove that way, she came as well - not in any hurry but just observing. Every now and then she’d stop and look around, and it looked like she was sniffing trying to find a trail (can cows do that?).

Bub wasn’t where we’d last seen him, so we kept searching and then I spotted a little white in amongst the reeds, yay!

Mum eventually got there too and they reunited - poor bub was very wobbly on his sore leg but managed to get up the hill to Mum to have a drink. After a little while, Mum started to leave and bub followed. Hopefully he’ll be OK!

We started heading back and I saw a fox on the hill near the main cow group - hopefully they’re all friends!

The weather had turned, it was very grey and getting cold. It rained just as we stepped inside and I said what great timing we had, but then Pete reminded me that we didn’t have firewood yet hehe luckily it’s so close to the house!

I called Keryn at Winning Appliances to follow up on the emails I’d sent 11 and 3 days ago - we were wanting to add another item to our quote, and also see if she could offer any discounts given the volume of our order. It turns out she hadn’t received the emails, d’oh! She added the dishwasher to our quote and said it was unlikely she could do much about the overall pricing, but would take a look and get back to us.

We got the joinery quote from Tod and it doens’t look too bad. Hopefully we’ll get the quote from Todd soon so we can compare.

The fridge man should be coming tomorrow, finally!

No human visitors yet, just orange bandits!

Nothing on the Bing Lee tracker either - I was doubtful they were actually coming. I remembered we had an ice container that should go back with the fridge/freezer, so I went to put it back in - grosssss, the inside was all mouldy now!! I was a bit worried they might penalise us instead of giving us a full refund, though it’s not really our fault considering they were supposed to pick it up last week.

So windy today!!

I finished my work morning and started preparing the bins to take out - of course that’s when the 3-man removalist team arrived! They preferred to park around the side instead of out the front. They were all friendly and the main man was very apologetic and appreciative of how understanding we’d been. Lots of water came out as they were lifting the fridge down from the porch, but otherwise there were no dramas and they were on their way again.

I drove the bins down in the buggy, then reversed back up - if the cement trucks could do it, I better have a go too haha

We headed up to see the cows, but as we got to the house site, we saw the white insulation material was all over the place. Lukas’ tool box had also blown open or been left open and his printed house plans were all wet. Pete moved the bigger bits of insulation and I collected the smaller bits - luckily not too many had blown outside the fence.

I threw some bits into the skip bin, but realised that might not have been the best idea as they might blow back out. So we took the next lot back to the house to dispose of - and took the house plans to lay out to dry.

Went to see the cows - they were all together. Wonkleg seemed OK. They didn’t all run off as quickly this time, but were still a bit standoffish.

On the way back, we were discussing where we might have our house paddock - Pete is certainly thinking much bigger than I was, we’ll need 4 Loobies to mow! hahaha

2:45 I made lunch and got back to work. Around 3:15 neighbour Pete visited and we had a chat - he had leant us his trundle wheel ages ago and needed it back.

Finally he mentioned again his mate’s name - Clarkey! I’d been waiting ages for him to say it as Pete and I had both forgotten and it felt too late to ask again especially after he’d done such a good turn for us mowing the roadside for us.

I got back to work until about 7, then spent some time rebalancing our finances from the end of the month. Did a bit more work and some journalling - it’s Week 11 and Pete is finally doing his contribution for Week 7 haha

Pete cut the pumpkin - it looked pretty good but we should have let it ripen more. We cooked a little bit in the air fryer and it didn’t taste too bad. But the next one will be even better I’m sure.

On Thursday we saw we had an overnight email from LMD -

We weren’t too worried about the delays…bit worried about how much those steel beams are going to cost though.

Headed into town at about 2pm, via Jacks Road for a scenic drive. Finally we could park on the grass at Woolies again - I’d hated having to park in the main carpark haha

We started doing a regular shop but it turned into a Big Shop for our monthly discount. $373!! I needed a lie down haha But apparently we saved $265 with all the weekly discounts and 10% off.

There was a new lady in the self-serve section and she made me bring the trolley all the way around instead of just passing things over the fence like we usually do, trying to stay out of the way haha actually there is room for a trolley in there now though, I’m sure there didn’t used to be.

Now that we had a trolley packed with things, it wasn’t convenient that I’d parked on the grass, so I drove around to the EV charging bays - was a bit worried about it as they’d just introduced fines for people parking there and not using the chargers. Someone had posted in one of the Gloucester Facebook groups that the fine was $2,200 but I think they were just scaremongering and it’s really only a couple of hundred bucks, but still. As I was parking Pete was flapping his arms about thinking I was going to bang the pole, but I was nowhere near it!! Though it’s worth noting - the Shark only beeps at you from corner sensors, so if there is a pole directly in front of you it’s certainly possible to hit it without any warning - though I was watching on the camera so all was fine this time.

Went for a drive over to King George’s park. The toilet block has been demolished - hopefully they’ll be replacing it. We had a walk over to the river walkway. The water was really high and flowing.

Back home at about 3:40, we took 10 to put some of the shopping away then headed to see the cows. Wonkleg is still with the group which is good. We have been trying to work out which cow is the leader of this group - maybe Horse Face but we’re not sure.

Have kept the fire going all day, it’s nice and cozy.

Mum and Dad will visit next weekend and bring the remaining lights, yay!

Not much happened on Friday morning, except bloody Looby kept getting stuck over near the garden beds for some reason, even though there didn’t appear to be anything in his way. Also it amused me how the pigeons were all lined up hehe

In sad news, I don’t think the coriander is going to make it :( Unfortunately I always seem to have mixed results with the Bunnings seedlings.

Keryn from Winning Appliances had called us yesterday and left a couple of emails trying to get in touch, and we finally got around to calling her back - she had felt bad about not being able to offer more of a discount to us given how many things we were buying, so she had spoken to her boss and been able to get a bigger discount on the fridge - it wasn’t much, but it was nice of her to try.

Headed out in the buggy - Pete’s Knobby underwear delivery I ordered had arrived. They have some pretty cool designs and when I buy them on the big sale they’re pretty reasonable (plus we got a free bag!)

Visited the cows and played them some music, including “3 Hours Classical Music For Cows Milk Production” hahaha

We debated whether we’d go to the markets on Saturday, and whether we’d buy any bread - I feel like they’re a bit pricy at $10-$15 a loaf, but they also look really good…

In the evening we watched the Roosters smash Canberra - it was the first time in 3 years we’d held a team scoreless, and the first time ever that we’d kept Canberra to 0. Marky Mark had a blinder with a hatrick in his first game back from injury.

Pete started making curry at around 4am on Sat. When he came to bed we decided we would try and go to the markets in Barrington later that morning - Pete would only get about 5hrs sleep though! In the end it wasn’t worth it as by the time we got there they’d already sold out of Anzac biscuits and bread, there were no booties for Mum and there was nothing else that took our fancy. Oh well, better luck next time - we’ll probably have to go even earlier!

We drove down Adele’s street and saw the highland cows. Drove around some of the neighbouring streets to see the houses and gardens. The main road was really busy, bloody out-of-towners! hehe

Headed to see how the Showground and nearby farms were looking - it was interesting seeing the hay all laid out.

Back in town, we parked and went to the Patisserie - they didn’t have any good bread either. We walked along the main street but didn’t buy anything, just admired all the visiting doggos.

We had a look in the gallery but the current exhibition wasn’t to our taste (photographs that were too over saturated).

As we walked past the Drifta they had a pallet leaning out the back and we asked the worker who was walking by if it might be available - she said no, but advised us to check their warehouse in the industrial area. We headed out that way but there were no pallets there either at the moment. We saw that the nursery was open, which was unusual - we headed in and I was surprised that they had such a great range and resonably priced. We bought a ‘Dorothy Gordon’ grevillea, which should have an interesting pinky/purple colour. Had a long chat with one of the owners, who seems nice - she mentioned that it didn’t look like there would be a Gloucester flower fair this year, which is a shame.

Woolies next. A couple of days ago when we were at the deli, we were chatting to the worker Gav, and Pete got one of the meat sticks off the counter and I joked “Where’s mine!” so he got me one too. Well today, Pete made a big deal of telling Gav that I hadn’t even eaten mine yet and Gav said ‘typical woman’ and they all had a big laugh and then Gav went on a big tirade about women hahah OK champ! haha nah he’s alright.

Finally Woolies had some good bread in stock - I guess I have those annoying out-of-towners to thank for the extra long-weekend stock hehe We also managed to finally save enough points to get the pot Bill wanted.

When we got home, I noticed with horror that our new grevillea was chopped in the car door! The next photo captures the damage and the culprit admitting responsibility haha luckily the plant wasn’t actually too badly damaged.

In other news, I read a post in one of the Gloucester Facebook groups where a lady was commending the hospital staff for looking after her when she sliced her finger. There were a few people saying they were surprised she wasn’t sent to Taree and she mentioned if it had needed stiches she would have been - are you kidding, our hospital can’t even do sticthes?! That seems hard to believe and is slightly concerning!

I had lunch while Pete sprayed the weeds on the driveway. At about 3:30 we headed for a cow visit.

I think I saw something jump out of the dam water twice! But we couldn’t see anything when we went for a closer look.

It looked like there had been some frost overnight.

I walked up to the house site and had a potter around the cottage while Pete waited for the water to heat back up so he could shower. I had spied a new orange flower from the kitchen window - closer up I realised it was actually 4 flowers! The passionfruit was also flowering again, hopefully we’d get some more fruit soon. An even more exciting discovery in the garden beds - bees!! Ever since we’d lived here, we’d never really seen any bees around, so this was a welcome breakthrough.

I was so proud I’d keep the fire going overnight, but then Pete informed me he’d wanted it to go out so he could clean out the ash, d’oh!

We headed in to town to see a garage sale that had been advertised. It was a deceased estate which was a bit sad - I gathered it was the children running the sale. It was a bit awkward as there was nothing there we were interested in.

Headed to Woolies next. A stupied out-of-towner was standing just inside the entrance, and when I triggered the two gates to open (which she couldn’t from that side because it’s a bloody entrance not an exit!) she started coming towards me, so I got out of the way - she just flounced on past and didn’t say sorry or thank you and then the fucking gate hit me, I was so cranky for the rest of the shop :(

We got some supplies to make pizza pastries for dinner that night.

Next we headed to IGA to see if they had any nice bread rolls for us to make eggy bacon rolls another night, but they were completely sold out. We tried the bakery but they weren’t even open on Sundays - lame!

We walked the back way back to the car and Pete excitedly pointed out a big screw haha

Back home I had lunch and later we headed down to check on the pumpkins. Spotted some pretty purple flowers (the photo is a bit deceiving, they were tiny).

I found one pumpkin that had been under water. The rest were looking good though.

We enjoyed the sounds of the birds and the creek.

We went to visit the cows. They were super friendly today. A lot of them, especially the bubs, came over to see what was happening.

I was a bit worried though, as I didn’t spot Wonkleg or his Mum.

We headed over to check on the natives. Clarkey had recently been over to mow between the plants and had done a fantastic job - where before it was getting quite overgrown with grass and weeds, it was now looking very tidy. We’ll have to invite him over for a beer one day.

Pete was very happy to find a walking stick hehe

Next we headed over to the top back paddock to see if maybe Wonkleg and his Mum were hiding anywhere but didn’t spot them. We said hello to the neighbour’s horse. We headed down along the fence line and found a part of the property we hadn’t visited before - it had heaps of bush rock! Very cool. We also found an interesting tree that had split.

We started heading back and had another look at the main group of cows, who were now over near one of the dams and heading up to the trees on the hill. Pete spotted Wonkleg - oh no, he wasn’t doing very well. I thought he had been getting better as he’d been running a bit more and putting more weight on the leg, but today he was very slowling hopping along and dragging his leg behind him. Poor bugger.

Back home I tried to catch up on last week’s journal and convince Pete to give me some missing info from three weeks ago haha

Spent some time looking at doors. I didn’t really like the one Pete had picked for our front door but there really weren’t many options that met our criteria. I found one that might be OK. Pete sent an email off to a couple of places to find out if they could do the morticing we needed and give us quotes. We got one quote back pretty quick - strange for a Sunday evening!

It felt like we were going stuff all weekend and never really got to relax - I was relieved to have a day off tomorrow for the King’s Birthday (interestingly my UK colleagues don’t get a holiday for the King’s Birthday!)

entry.title: Build Week 10
entry.content:
No early visitors on Monday.

Saw we had an email from Todd the kitchen man -

Uhh…that’s not a question? Also a bit surprised he was so negative instead of trying to offer a solution or an alternative. Oh well.

Went out in the Shark in my break - I was hopeless at driving again :(

We saw some info in the Shark dash and Pete did some calculations - I think he said our energy use so far was $21 per 1000km? Maybe he’ll share some more insights.

No doggos in the park, sad. Headed to Woolies but couldn’t park in our usual grass spot as it was too boggy.

Had a little drive down Mograni Creek Rd - saw lots of cows and a bunny rabbit.

Pete suggested going to Taree on Tuesday, booooo. He was also hassling me to do the BYD survey - I didn’t really want to because I think they’re stupid when they tell you “oh anything less than a 9 and I’ll get in trouble” like guilt-tripping you into only writing positive things and so what’s the point. Also I was annoyed because I’d emailed Marty about the original tyres (which I felt we were entitled to as they were included in the main price, before we upgraded them) and he said he’d find out but then he ghosted me. But anyway, Pete was hassling me to do the survey because he wanted to win $10K but when I clicked the link I was a day too late :(

I made lunch and got back to work around 2:45. Pete called the other kitchen Tod (yes the kitchen guys are called Todd and Tod haha) to see if we could come in on Tuesday - he wasn’t available for the next few days, but we arranged to meet on Friday.

I spent some time getting fridge things organised ahead of the pick-up on Wedneday. Made room in the outside fridge by putting some less-necessary items in a crate and lugging them back inside. Then emptied the inside fridge - moved some non-perishable things to the floor in the kitchen, moved some things to the fridge outside, and had to throw a bunch out - some was best before 2025?! Not sure how that happened.

Got back to work and then Pete called me from outside - he’d spotted a hare in the long grass just outside our side fence.

Back to work until 7:30, then tried to research some more doors. Not much progress.

We did the wash-ups then I made pizza pastry scrolls for dinner.

Now we had consolidated the fridge items, we no longer had room for the huge 1/2 watermelon we still had left. We ate some then put it out under the tree out the front - maybe the possum would visit again?

On my morning check of the cameras on Tuesday, I saw Lukas and someone arrived at 7:37, transporting an interesting yellow box.

I couldn’t see any camera evidence of a possum visit :(

I thought Lukas might just be here for a quick inspection, but he didn’t leave until about midday.

Pete moved the empty fridge out to the porch, ready to be picked up tomorrow.

I spent some time transferring my monthly salary into our various accounts and paying some bills.

A truck with some crusher dust arrived at 2:20 - bloody tore up the grass again haha Pete went up to the house site to open the gate for him.

We spent some time in the garden. The butterflies were loving the Marigolds!

Decided to have a quick walk up to see what had changed on the building site - well I decided to walk, but Pete was lazy and took the buggy and just kept driving behind me and tooting haha

We could see the crusher dust delivery, there was a new yellow toolbox and the next lot of formwork had begun. There were also some interesting pink things I hadn’t noticed before - apparently they hold the formwork boards in place while the concrete is poured.

Headed back down and had a look at the state of our poor driveway and grass. A bit sad, but not unexpected :)

Prepared my lunch and ate at my desk at 3:15 while I did another work shift - was planning to do 3 shifts today so I could take some time off on Friday for the Taree trip.

As I was working my evening shift, I thought I saw the fridge cord move. It might just have been a coincidence, but shortly after I went to the door and called out to the possum just in case he was around - there he was right in the tree in front of us! He stared at us for a bit then went to hide up in the higher branches.

Pete had forgotten to do his drone shot of the new house site yesterday, so he did one at 6:30am then came to bed.

It was busy this morning - Lukas arrived with a digger at 7:09. Then a white Isuzu at 7:12, another white Isuzu and trailer at 7:15, a black 4WD (a vehicle we hadn’t seen before!) and trailer also at 7:15, and a white Hilux at 7:16.

The fridge man called - they’d had some sort of bingle in the truck and needed to replace a mirror - he asked if he could come another day and we agreed Friday would be fine.

The pest man arrived at 11. He has been quite a few times, I’d love to know what he’s doing! I can only hope he’s been installing some super spider defence system haha

Someone left at midday and came back 20mins later - probably to get something for lunch? But it was quite a quick trip.

I finally saw the new red train!! After a year off the tracks for major upgrades, the service between Sydney and Grafton resumed on Tues 28th April with a fancy new red XPT - I wondered why it took so long for me to see one, but I think the train services some other routes (Sydney <–> Melbourne, Sydney <–> Dubbo) as well. The picture isn’t great, but I was excited hehehe

I finally got around to trying a ‘Papple’ - Woolies had had them for a while but they were a bit pricey so I’d been reluctant to try one. Google says a papple is “a unique hybrid fruit that looks like an apple but has the crisp texture, juiciness, and sweetness of a pear. Developed in New Zealand from a cross between European and Asian pears…” I LOVE asian/nashi pears, so it sure sounded like a winner. I wasn’t disappointed but the price at $2 seemed a bit steep…though I think I’m still in denial about how much everything costs these days. Apples are maybe $1.60 each? I feel like they should be half that haha I guess my brain is living in the past haha

The pest man left at 12:30 - lucky he escaped before it started pouring! The other workers stuck it out for a bit, but left between 1:15 - 1:30.

Pete and I headed in to town about 1:20 - first to IGA to get some buns for dinner. Then we headed up to the lookout to see what the view was like with the low cloud cover.

Got some disappointing post - Transport for NSW had rejected Pete’s application for an exemption to drive the Shark.

Online advice seems to imply that people who have no other means of transport to access basic services (e.g. grocery shopping) should be able to receive an exemption. We wondered if they’d actually been able to read Pete’s handwriting. Or if we’d applied too soon after we changed the Scooby registration and they still thought that vehicle was available at this residence. Oh well. I guess I will be chauffeur for the next…15 months? Can’t remember exactly when Pete will be off his Ps but it’s bloody ages away haha

Around 3pm I made a lunch snack and got back to work until 4:30, when Pete did his drone shot and we headed up to the house site to see the latest. It was getting even more boggy. Pete was naughty and ran through the house hehe

Had a quick cow visit, then headed back just as it started to rain again.

Back to work again. Oh no, forgot I had more chores I was meant to do earlier! I watered the porch plants, watered the indoor plants and planted the rocket in my new pots (like the orange/black ones Pete had made, but these had a blue highlight). The water measurer is interesting, I am not convinced how well it works yet.

Bacon and Egg rolls for dinner while watching State of Origin :D

No early visitors on Thursday morning.

Saw a Facebook post from Kym, one of the workers we know from Woolies.

When Pete woke up I asked if we could offer our help and he agreed. I saw a few people had already responded positively, but when I said we could drop by around 2-3 that arvo if that suited her, she picked us, yay!

First Pete moved the gargoyle a short distance, which was easy.

See that item in the background - I think that’s what my brain pictured as the other item we’d have to move, though that’s clearly a bird bath and not a fountain haha but I was thinking roughly that size for some reason. I thought it was something Pete and I would be able to lift together. Well it turns out it was a huge 2-tiered thing, maybe 80cm diameter at its widest and about 1.2m high - and it was still full of water! haha This was not going to be a quick job haha

First we moved a table out of the way, then Pete carefully removed the Angel statue off the top of the fountain - that on its own was really heavy. Then he removed the top basin, the stand, and then we were left with the larger basin which we started bucketing the water out of. Once it got a bit lower we were able to tip the rest of the water out but it was hard work making sure the basin didn’t slip off the base. Then Pete lifted the basin off - it was incredibly heavy and I think he was at his limits. Unfortunately I couldn’t really help because of the awkward shape and I would have just gotten in the way.

Kym was very friendly and we all had a good chat while Pete was doing most of the work. She seems very proud of her place and was excited about moving the fountain a bit to make more room for the BBQ and future guests. We also got to see her budgie Romeo. Kym was really grateful for Pete’s help and offered us a plant and a small table but we declined.

Pete moved the base of the fountain about 30cm closer into the corner, then got to assembling everything again1. It was hard work and I felt helpless! He almost let me help with the last bit - it was tricky because the angel had a bit of pipe coming out, that was bent/squashed but needed to align with a hole in the stand underneath.

Pete was hoping I could help line things up but then he decided he could do it all himself, such a show-off hehe

Kym was very happy and insisted we take a big bag of chocolates and lollies - couldn’t say no to that hehe

When we got home and I went to plug in the charger, I saw that last time we had the panel open a bird must have pooped inside there - what a little bugger!!

In other bird news, I noticed that some of the leftover bird seed near the feeder has started growing through the wood!

I made a little diagram for the fridge man in case he arrived while we were in Taree tomorrrow.

We were getting heaps of rain - Pete had to tape the pipe near the tank, and the gutter out the front was overflowing - Pete put a bin underneath it and it quickly filled up.

I had a bit of a restless sleep Thurs night / Fri morn, and had been moving around a lot. The bed was quite warm when Pete came to bed, which I thought would be a positive thing but he joked “It’s like getting in a pool someone peed in” hahaha how rude!

The fridge man called - with all the rain, and the photo I’d sent yesterday, he was worried about getting bogged and suggested we delay the pick-up. He said he’d message us on Sunday to see how the weather was doing, and possibly come next Monday or Wednesday.

I worked a couple of hours in the morning, then just before 11 we headed to Taree. It was still raining a lot and I thought I was driving to the conditions but at one point I noticed Pete was unusually quiet and I asked him if it was because he was stressed about my driving and he said Yes! He reckoned it was the most ‘agressive’ I’d ever driven (not just this car, but ever!) I hadn’t thought I was driving badly, but I guess I’m still getting used to the car :(

First stop was Manning Freight to pick up Pete’s floor boxes - oh yeah, we finally found out what happened to them and it turned out we had to pick them up from Taree rather than them being delivered the rest of the way - though it sounds like the couriers might be allowed to deliver to Gloucester again soon.

I drove a little up the road so Pete could look at a door place - I had a grumbly belly so had to rush to the servo down the road. Luckily it was quite a decent bathroom! Pete said the door place was no good and walked a bit down the road to Lear & Smith who had electical, lighting and data supplies. I met him there. He was able to get positive answers to most of his questions and was going to email the man more info so he could get a quote on a few things.

By the time we finished there, it was maybe 12:30 and our appointment with Tod at the kitchen place was at 1pm. Pete looked up the business and noticed it wasn’t actually open today, uh-oh! But luckily Tod was opening up just to meet with us and he said he was already there and we could head over, winner!

Tod’s “Concept Design Kitchens & Joinery” was on Pulteney St which was quite a main road with lots of people coming and going - I was a bit worried someone would ding the Shark but there wasn’t much I could do.

We met Tod and showed him the piece of flooring sample and talked through our current ideas. He had printed our plans and emails and asked us a lot of questions to try and understand what to recommend and what needed quoting. We didn’t know how to answer everything but he helped guide us and we settled on a few things to be quoted. We discussed the likely difficulty in being able to source a countertop at the size we wanted. Instead of having a join in the one material, he suggested we could do one section in the stone we wanted and then a deliberately different material - he recommended a wood block which we thought was a good idea and could work well. We looked at some bench samples and thought the Grafite Titanio was close to what we had in mind (definitely preferring a matte, darker tone, with a minimal pattern.) Then we looked at wood samples - we had a few we didn’t mind, but liked the Tasmanian Oak Matt the best. Instead of wood for all joinery, we also discussed possibly having the main island in Eucalypt.

We spent about an hour there and it was very productive. We were quite impressed with Tod and were hoping the quote he came back with would be something we could work with!

As we headed back to the car, we got a whiff of the Charcoal Chicken shop we’d parked out the front of, and decided to get some chippies. Unfortunately they were way over salted! I didn’t want to waste them so I still ate some haha We parked down by the water while I ate and we considered our next move - no nice river views though as it was raining again and the windows were all fogged up haha

I was trying to get Pete to tell me all the home building supply stores he wanted to visit, so we could make the most of our trip, but he was apathetic because of the weather. So we went to Manning Mall to go to Coles and the butcher to get some things for dinner. I had wanted to visit the Taree Central shopping centre as well, as we hadn’t been there before, but after looking up exactly what shops were there, I wasn’t really convinced anymore. But we went anyway haha Pete looked in EB Games and I looked in Big W and bought a cheap shirt and fluffy jacket for around the house.

We decided to try a couple of door places before we headed home, but one was closed and the other one only had aluminium doors, no good.

Pete said I drove much better on the way back!

We headed to the post office when we got back to Gloucester, as Pete had a delivery to pick up. I thought it would be interesting to see how the rivers were looking after all the rain - we weren’t disappointed! Where we normally park on the Relfs Rd boat ramp, to admire the view, it was completely under water! The Barrington River was rushing along. The rain had stopped at least, and the sky was looking pretty with the setting sun.

Next we headed to Gloucester District Park and the Gloucester River was huge and running fast there as well. We went for a walk along the river until we couldn’t go any further as the path was under water!

We got home at about 5:30 and I did another couple of hours work before wrapping up for the weekend.

On Saturday as I had my morning walk around the house, I could hear the creek running - hopefully our pumpkins hadn’t been washed away!

Good and bad news around the cottage garden. On the plus side it looked like some daffodils or jonquils were strating to sprout, and the butterflies were putting on a show with the marigolds. Unfortunately the first watermelon that grew, was now rotting :(

I spent some time going through Mum’s shortlist of properties for Norfolk Island, reviewing them some more and adding them to our comparison spreadsheet. I added my thoughts and some rankings.

Pete and I headed down to check on the pumpkins at about 1:45. Thankfully they looked mostly unharmed by the recent weather. Except for the vine that had previously trailed across the creek bed - that was now thoroughly under water! It looked like the creek had been over one of the banks but the water had gone down now.

We inspected the biggest/best pumpkin and thought he was looking good - we researched the characteristics of a ripe pumpkin and he seemed to match, so we gave him a chop. There were quite a few others coming along, including this double-decker we just discovered.

Saw a cool mushroom near where we’d parked the buggy - boot for scale hehe

A quick trip up to the house site, and Pete spotted more interesting mushrooms on the way back.

I’d worn my new fluffy jumper and I don’t know when it happened but I must have rubbed against some plants and now I had sticky plant bits all over me - really hard to remove and they were pulling out bits of jumper with them, so annoying!!

Made some lunch at about 2:15 and spent more time on the Norfolk Island accommodation planning. It was hard to decide what criteria were most important to us. Was it the views? Or good location and surroundings? Did we want to be close to town or more secluded? One place that was high up our list had a lot of complaints about potholes making the access road almost undriveable. Some of the places advertised remarkable views, but the photo evidence was lacking. For places with multiple cabin types and locations, it was hard to ascertain which of them (if any) had the better views. And what about the layout? We thought we found a gem, but then realised it had a tiny kitchen table and only 1 couch for 4 guests! We were getting closer to making a decision though and had a pretty good shortlist - Channers, Shearwater, Routi House and Endeavour Lodge.

Later I spent some time taking everything out of the fridge outside and carting it inside, so Pete could move the fridge in. Then he cleaned the top and I cleaned the inside. How did it get so dirty and full of bugs in just a few months!! I re-stocked everything and it was looking good. What a joy to have a working inside fridge again!

More Norfolk planning and then some garden chores - I took out some of the marigold that had died and planted the remaining snapdragons. Pete spent some time rolling the driveway again so poor Looby wouldn’t have to struggle over the rough terrain haha

Sunday morning, and I wasn’t initially planning to do more Norfolk Island research but I saw Mum had sent me her revised shortlist so I started looking into our top picks a bit more. One of the things I noticed was that Channers didn’t really have anywhere you could sit outside, vs Endeavour that had the lovely deck. We were all pretty keen on Endeavour so I suggested I book it as there was only one 2-bedroom cottage, and if I booked it on Booking.com we could cancel it for free until late January if we changed our minds. Mum and Dad both agreed to go ahead and book it so I did. There was a funny moment, while I was going ahead with the booking, when Mum messaged me “Is it this one?” haha You can’t say that after you already said to go ahead! Luckily we were all talking about the same place haha

Once that was booked, I thought I’d check how the flights were looking, to make sure they weren’t selling out. Our preferred/cheapest dates were still available, and there was a sale price, but it wasn’t refundable. So we had to be sure. We decided to go ahead and book it!

I had a hell of a time trying to navigate the million steps - added travel insurance, tried to pick seats but it was being very temperamental, woke Pete up to decide if he wanted to sit in an aisle or window, put everyone’s names and details in, tried to get to the payment step but got a “Sorry an error seems to have occurred…” Waaaaah! I had to start again, but luckily it had saved some of the passenger details. And as a plus, the second flight, that previously I couldn’t select seats for, now let me pick them. The payment step was a bit confusing as there were so many options and they all had fees except for BPay. I didn’t really want to pay, I think it was $88 extra just to use my card, so I went for BPay - the only downsides were that I couldn’t BPay the travel insurance and also the payment wouldn’t go through straight away so I’d have to wait for the confirmation. I paid the travel insurance on card and sent through the BPay for the flights - they say you have until midnight to make the payment, so I figured I’d find out tomorrow if it was all confirmed. I needed a lie down haha We were all excited for the trip though! Except Pete who I think was still a bit confused about everything that was going on hehe

Did some chores then planned to head into town. As we got to the bottom of the driveway, we noticed the gate was closed. Oh no - had Pete moved the cows? As we drove up the road we saw the side paddock gate was open so he must have taken 240 and the others across to his place. Sad. Later we checked the cameras and you could just see the cows behind the tree, being herded down the road.

We had a drive out Bulliac Creek way - we’d driven out there only once before but it was a lovely area we’d planned to visit again once we got a more appropriate car. Actually the dirt road is not too bad, but we thought it would just be better in a 4wd. There are lots of open paddocks with cows grazing and beautiful hilly scenery. We saw a couple with a dog, out for a walk - we figured they were staying at the tiny home ‘Mowgli’. Cheapest I could see was $275 a night, with a minimum 2 night stay. Pretty steep I thought, though it was a nice spot.

We parked just near there as it was the end of the council maintained road and there was a sign advising of a locked gate ahead - we weren’t sure how far ahead but we didn’t want to risk not being able to turn around. We had a little walk to see what we could see. The cows were all around - we hoped they were friendly! As we walked around one bend, we could see the road seemed to go on for quite some way. Maybe we would walk or drive further another time. We could see Bundook Rd in the valley and tried to get our bearings for where we were looking - possibly near the spot we drove in a tunnel next to the railway one time - we would have to investigate from that angle soon.

Drove back to Kia Ora Rd then out to the end that looks out towards our property - we can see our build site now!!

We also saw some cows having a scratch.

Headed back into town and visited IGA, Woolies and then got some petrol for the Shark and the buggy (the latter with our jerry can). We’d forgotten to visit a garage sale yesterday, so I thought I’d drive by and see if they had any leftovers out the front, but no luck.

As we were driving over the train track on the way out of town, Pete noticed an interesting phenomenon where some smoke from a nearby chimney had risen into the sky then cooled and was now sitting in a little pool on the track, it looked really unusual but I don’t think we got a pic of it.

As we were driving past our place just after 5, I thought I spotted one cow in the paddock - oh no, had one gotten left behind? We parked the Shark and quickly took the buggy to have a look before it got too dark. Luckily it wasn’t one cow, but lots of cows, yay! It was a new group with some bubs, how exciting - we’d have to come for a proper visit tomorrow!

As a last highlight of the day, Pete made a new taste sensation for dinner - mashed potato with oregano in it!

1 - A couple of weeks later Kym advertised in one of the Facebook groups about a plant she was giving away, and the fountain was in the background of the photo, so now you can get a better idea of what it looks like and the (small!) distance we had to move it.

entry.title: Build Week 09
entry.content:
Nobody arrived early this morning. Someone and a passenger arrived at 11:30 and left 40mins later - we think it was probably the concreter and Lukas.

Pete got an email about the floor boxes - he thought they might have finally been delivered so he went down in the buggy to check, but it was just his new phone case.

I took a slightly earlier break today. As we prepared to drive into town, it was rainy and miserable - then we remembered we can make toasty warm car seats now, what a luxury! We had a quick trip to see what doggos were at the park. Then to Woolies - we were after some Wombok but there wasn’t any, but one of the staff overhead us discussing it and went out the back to cut one for us, how nice! Spoke to Stacey at the checkout - she was in pain as she’d recently hurt her shoulder at work. She said she was having trouble getting compo and we agreed she should take the arvo off!

We drove home via Jacks Rd - Pete made me turn around to see a cool digger hehe

Later in the arvo, Pete thought maybe he’d missed the floor boxes earlier so went down in the buggy to check again. They weren’t there - I think he’s just looking for excuses to go out in the buggy hahaha

Pete got some feedback on his spider Facebook post - I think there was some initial discussion around it possibly being a funnelweb or a mouse spider, but the consensus seemed to be that it was a ‘Badumna’ or Black House Spider, which with much relief we found out is not too dangerous. Though the advice for Australians is generally - if bitten by a big black spider, just assume it’s a funnelweb and act accordingly until proven otherwise!

Pete has started printing some more pots for me, after he dried out the filament last night.

For dinner we had pork that Pete marinated, along with some cabbage salad in a wrap. The pork was absolutely delicious and it was a really good combination - hopefully it wasn’t a fluke!

We watched some more Eurovision but only got through another 10 songs - still 5 to go!

We had visits from Mick, the concreter and Lukas this morning. Lukas called Pete and told him he was going to put in the extra drainage Pete had requested that the plumber had complained about haha

The team were doing the last prep before the first concrete pour tomorrow, and so Pete and I were planning to head into town a bit earlier than usual to see if the floor boxes were at the post office, in case they would be helpful (though we knew the measurements so they weren’t essential). But Lukas left at 11:30 and Mick about 15mins later, so we thought we’d missed our opportunity.

We saw that we had an email from Todd about the kitchen, and Pete put a response together -

Mick came back at 1pm so the post office trip was back on! We also planned to take the cans to Return and Earn - for the first time in the Shark! As we were preparing, Lukas arrived and we had a good chat. Everything was looking fine for the pour the next day, though he said the concreter could still call in the morning and cancel if the weather turned. We spoke about the difficulty getting people to deliver out of town and he said sometimes he’s able to get things delivered to Mitch at Gloucester Valley Landscape Supplies which is handy!

We finished loading the boxes of cans into the Shark, and Pete secured everything with tarp so nothing would blow away. The Post Office was our first stop, but there were no floor boxes, boooo - we’re not sure what’s happened to them. While he was waiting at the PO, Pete had a call from Mick and a message from Nick - hectic! Mick wanted to check how many conduits he needed to run for the solar guys and what size they were - he was just being thorough and making sure they’d all fit, so Pete called Tim while we were returning the cans and passed on some more details and everything was fine.

Now we can transport more cans, it was our biggest haul yet - $23.90 for cans and 30c for bottles!

Visited Circle of Friends to check out their new shop (they’d just relocated down the block) - it was fine but I preferred the layout of their old shop better.

We visited Nick to pick up a piece of the sander that had been forgotten the other day.

Back home, we headed up to check out the latest - the last electrical prep before the slab is poured including holes for the floor boxes (white) and more conduit (orange). It’s so muddy up there at the moment!

A quick buggy over to see the cows, who were over near the middle gates - nice and close today. 240 was really friendly but didn’t want any pats today. I think she was a bit disappointed I hadn’t brought any treats.

Back home, I was reviewing what items I had left to plant - oops, I’d missed one of the cauliflower punnets the other day! I planted it over in one of the garden beds. I also planted the Callisia Pink Panther in the yellow pot I’d bought from neighbour David in his moving sale, planted the Fittonia in the cute doggo V&B had given me, and the coriander in Pete’s new printed pot - which fit perfectly on the new stand!

Wednesday and the big day had arrived - the first pour!

Lukas got here first at 6:20. The plumber arrived at 6:25 and left at 6:50 - I believe he came to pressurise the heating system so the concrete could be poured without damaging the pipes.

The workers started arriving closer to 7. The pest guy came at 7:05 and left at 7:38 - not sure what he was up to. The concreters arrived at 7:12 and 7:26. A big noisy pump truck arrived at 7:45.

The first cement truck arrived at 8:08 - it went up to the shed, but then went back to turn around on the grass out the front of the house, then reversed up to the house site.

The second cement truck arrived at 8:17 - it went up to the shed, then turned around, tearing up the driveway and grass a bit. It waited for the first truck to be done.

The third truck arrived at 8:50 and parked on the grass out the front.

As a truck would finish at the site, it would come back down to the side of the house, letting the next truck pass and reverse up to the house site, before itself reversing back up next to the side of the shed - we thought perhaps to clean its chute into the ditch, though I didn’t really see any evidence of that. Whatever they were doing, they usually left about 5 minutes later.

The first swap happened around 9 - truck 2 went up to the site. Truck 1 left at 9:05 and truck 3 moved to in front of the shed.

I noticed truck 4 and truck 5 were waiting down on Bundook road.

Truck 2 left at 9:25.

At 9:29 truck 4 came up to park at the shed, then truck 5 came up to park out the front of the house.

Truck 5 headed up and truck 4 left at 9:56.

Around 10am, Lukas invited us up (actually he’d called Pete earlier but we hadn’t realised). As I stepped outside I spotted a poor sick rat on the grass. He was so cute, I felt bad that he must have eaten the poison :(

We headed up to the house site in the buggy. It was so exciting!!

I took some pictures from outside the fence, but then Lukas saw us and called us over - we had a bit of a chat and he said things were going well, but he was a bit stressed earlier as the pump had had a blockage and they couldn’t get things started, which was why the trucks had started to back up.

It was great seeing all the work that had already been done, and all the work in progress.

We started to head back, but then spotted truck 6 reversing up the driveway, so thought we’d wait and see him start to unload. He took his time and my arm was aching from holding the camera for so long haha

We headed back home. I gave poor cute ratty his last meal and then got back to work.

Show-off trucks 7 and 8 reversed the whole way up the driveway hahaha

Truck 9 was the last to arrive at 12:27 and left at 12:51

Here is a rough timeline of all the trucks arriving at the house, the waiting period and departure times.

Pete used his roller to try and flatten some of the grass and driveway back out, after it had been damaged by all the heavy trucks. He did a pretty good job!

At 1pm the pump truck came down and turned around then headed back up. Not really sure why!

We headed into town to run some errands at 1:20 and got back at 2:40. We noticed Lukas had put a sign on the fence now too :)

Lukas had left while we were out and the rest of the workers left between 3:19 - 3:26. The concreter stopped for a quick chat with Pete.

Around 4, Pete took a drone shot then we headed up to have a look.

Had a visit with the cows, but 240 and Bella were very disappointed with the garlic wrap I’d brought.

We received a quote for the flooring, and it looks like it’s considerably cheaper than what was budgeted in the LMD quote (about $45K), woohoo!

What a day! Here’s a quick recap of some of the action.

On Thursday I had my morning walk around the garden - a couple of the new caulis were looking a bit sick and a few capsicums were a bit chewed. On the plus side, quite a few more tomatoes were growing.

Our excitement yesterday that something had finally come under budget - that was short-lived haha it turns out the $45K quote also included the hydronic floor heating, which was a considerable amount.

But the good news is, we’re not over budget. And the cheaper of the two floor options (based on board size) was the one we preferred.

Pete started printing me a new fancy pot with a little watering section (pics to come later).

Mum and Dad asked what was happening with the fridge and I told them the whole saga. Dad started sending me all sorts of info about my rights and how we were entitled to a refund, which I knew already. But he also found some info that said it was the supplier’s responsibility to pick up the item - I wasn’t sure about this, seeing we were out of their delivery range. But the info did seem to indicate that for heavy items that were difficult to transport, the consumer is not responsible for returning it in order to obtain the refund. Interesting. I didn’t really want to bring it up with Pete again as I knew it would cause another argument.

Another spanner in our plans - Pete discovered that the Shelly Pro 2pm Dimmers, that he’d ordered 22 of, didn’t have the RCM mark they needed, to be permitted for installation in Australia. They did have a related certificate, but Pete wasn’t sure that would suffice - he’d have to check with Mick.

I was awake half the night with cramps and stressing about the fridge. I was planning to get in touch with Bing Lee, and had been lying awake planning all the things I’d say, so I asked Pete to forward me the previous correspondence. Instead I woke up to an email from him volunteering me to return the fridge on Saturday 2hrs away. We don’t even know if it fits in the Shark yet, or how the hell we’re going to get it in there! I was even more stressed now.

I tried to do my morning of work, while constantly checking my emails to see if Bing Lee had replied, while I waited for Pete to wake up so we could discuss things. When he awoke, he thought the whole thing was terribly funny - it turns out he hadn’t sent that email to Bing Lee, but he had saved it as a draft weeks ago, and when he forwarded me the rest of the emails it had sent that one as well (but only to me). So much relief - I didn’t have to waste my Saturday or risk damage to the Shark!

Pete reluctantly agreed that I could deal with the fridge now - it was all my responsibility and he was wiping his hands of it. Fair enough.

I realised that the previous correspondence was already quite in our favour actually (which made it even more preposterous why Pete kept saying I was trying to be difficult!!) - the lady had already suggested a refund would be possible, and also talked about ‘pick up’ of the fridge. So I didn’t even need my carefully formulated lines about ‘our rights’ I just replied steering her towards things she’d already suggested and 20 mins and a couple of emails later she’d confirmed a refund would be processed after the fridge was received, and that someone from Taree would be coming to pick it up next Wednesday. Woohoo!

I gave Vicki a heads up in case anyone from Bing Lee called, and I said that the refund was likely to go back to her card, as her and Bill had originally made the purchase for us. Pete reluctantly acknoweledged my victory -

He won’t say it, but I’m SURE he must be glad he doesn’t have to lift the bloody thing up into the ute!!

In more positive news, now that we weren’t getting a credit for a dishwasher, I contacted Winnings (who we are buying a bunch of other appliances through) who have the same model dishwasher for the same price - but unlike Bing Lee who won’t deliver to us, Winnings will - so I’ve saved a future trip as well, yay!

Headed up to the house site in the arvo to see how it was looking after the rain. I also thought it was interesting to see what was in the skip bin so far hehe

I can’t remember what else we did on Friday except that Pete did a fantastic job fixing the buggy screen. It had been a bit wonk ever since we got it - whenever you tried to close it, the bits didn’t line up properly. I’ll admit I wasn’t confident he could fix it, but it didn’t take long at all and it’s perfect now!

On Saturday I was at my desk when some galahs put on a show - I think it’s the first time I’ve seen any of the birds here mating, which is very surprising given how many there are.

I know February is a long way off, but I asked Mum if she’d thought any more about what she might like to do for her 80th next year - just so we could start getting some ideas together and book some things if they needed booking. I started putting a spreadsheet together of possible locations for a NSW trip, and also looked at the possibility of flying to Norfolk Island and spending a week there.

That afternoon, Vicki mentioned that her and Bill were looking to come up tomorrow for lunch. Yay - but oh no, I wish I’d done more chores that morning instead of trip planning!

Pete and I spent the next couple of hours tidying the kitchen and lounge room and vacuuming, to make things a bit more presentable.

I also planted the Parsley in the fancy pots Pete printed. You can pour water in the small triangle bit, the water then sits at the bottom (under the orange section) for the plant to absorb when needed. The little orange stick floats when that section is full of water, and will lower so you know when to add more. In other news, we spotted that Looby had lost a bit off his wheel - we’ll have to order some more.

Next we planned to head into town to wash the car and get some supplies for V&Bs visit. But oh no - the car was dead? None of the buttons in the car or on the key seemed to be doing anything, it was completely unresponsive. Pete Googled to see what might be happening, and apparently it was just asleep and I just needed to press the button on the outside door handle a number of times to wake it up. Weird, but OK!

We headed off. I’d bought $2 with me, telling Pete he could use it at the car wash so we wouldn’t be locked into the $5 minimum increments for card payments. He found my frugality amusing and just put $20 straight on :(

While Pete was washing the car, a bloke (the carwash owner or just a passerby?) came over and gave him some advice about the best order to wash…which seemed counter-intuitive but who knows. We didn’t end up using the full amount we paid for and Pete let some rando stranger use the rest.

Headed to Woolies for groceries. We debated what to have for dinner and Pete suggested he could make Bolognese again, but I told him absolutely not as I’d just cleaned the stove ahead of V&Bs arrival and his messy meal would have to wait! haha

Up early Sunday so we could do some last chores before V&B arrived around Midday. Had lunch and a good catch up before heading out in the buggy. First we headed down to the creek to see how the pumpkins were doing. Then up to the house site - it was pretty boggy. Next we drove through the paddocks, across the creek and over to see the KoalaWays planting area - a few of the plants were looking a bit dead, but most were looking good. Then a quick trip to say hello to the cows before heading back to the cottage.

Back home, we had more of a chat then Vicki got serious. Uh-oh. The main reason for the visit, other than to see us and the house site progress, was to let us know some bad news - she’d gotten some test results that indicated diffuse atheroma and probable severe stenosis in her Left Anterior Descending artery - in layman’s terms, a build-up of plaque and narrowing of the arteries supplying the heart with blood, which was obviously very serious. I believe she has to wait a month and then they’ll decide on next steps - but surgery for stenting may be necessary.

A troubling end to the week, but we are all hoping for a good outcome.

Later that night, Pete and I spent some time looking at the doors he’d shortlisted. He’d been pretty frustrated with the available options. I didn’t like the one he’d picked for our main front door, but was happy with the others. Sadly, we found more things that had been missed from the quote - 2 external doors (from the dining hall to the undercover area that may be a lounge/media room in future) and we noticed that there’s no allocation at all for any flyscreens for windows or doors. Great!

entry.title: Build Week 08
entry.content:
It was all happening at the site today! So many different vehicles coming and going. First was a plumber and a grey Hilux at about 6:50. Then Lukas and a little truck arrived at 7:30 - they left about an hour later.

We finally had a sprinkling of rain! The Willies were enjoying themselves. At about 9:30, the plumber left and a black Holden Ute went up, but left about 5 mins later. The plumber was back again about 10:15.

Now neighbour Pete had burnt off his paddock, the next step was seeding it via drone.

Precision Pest Services were next to arrive, shortly after 11. They left a bit under an hour later. Lil Fish, our electrician Mick, arrived at about 1pm and Lukas arrived in a different truck at about quarter past.

Mick and his offsider came down to the shed and asked Pete to go up to the house site. Along with Lukas, they had a chat about where some of the services were going.

A white Ute went up at 1:37 and left about ten minutes later. Pete later told me it was the concreter come to collect his forgotten lunchbox - Pete and I had spotted it on the weekend and joked that we should sneak a snack in it hehe

Mick left at about 2:20, and the grey hilux, the plumber and Lukas all left at about 3:10. In total there were 9 different vehicles on site today!

Pete and I headed up at about 4 to see the progress - the hydronic heating had started to go in, which looked pretty cool. They had quite an elaborate system to mark it all out.

The plumber and a grey Hilux (probably the plumber’s offsider) arrived at 6:50 on Tuesday, and left about 3 hours later.

It was raining again today, which is good news for the newly-planted natives.

A white Ute arrived at 11:20 and left about 5 mins later - not sure who that was, but we think it might have been the concreter.

Pete bought a new toy off Nick.

When we headed up to the house site for our afternoon sticky-beak, we saw that more pipes for the hydronic heating had gone in.

We had a new email from Penny -

Bloody additional costs. Bit annoying the engineers hadn’t included all the relevant detail the first time!

Pete made a new moth friend -

Nobody on the building site on Wednesday.

We had an early email from Kristy from the council -

That was lovely and generous, though part of me was a bit worried about having to plant and water another 30 shrubs when we were struggling to manage the ones we had already. On the plus side, hopefully the ground would be a little softer after the recent rain.

In other news, it turns out Todd from Viison had replied to our April email about cabinetry, but for some reason Pete’s email forwarding system hadn’t worked and we never saw it. But things were progressing and he would likely send us a quote next week.

Headed in to town - one of the benefits of being the driver now, is that Pete has to take the bins out, ner ner haha

Went to the hardware store to get another extension cord. Called Kristy to see if it was easier for her to meet us in town rather than coming to our place, but she said she was back at home now - she’d be back in to town later to pick up her kids and would come see us then.

We headed home via Jacks Rd and saw some nice Autumn trees and cows.

We stopped in to check on our natives and see how the ground was looking in preparation for the next planting.

Back home, Pete did some work to staple some of the shed electrical cable to the roof so the birds wouldn’t be able to sit on it to poop on the Shark as much.

Made my lunch and sat down to work, and shortly after saw a car driving away - oh no, I’d missed Kristy! I hadn’t heard or seen her arrive and Pete thought I was just hiding!

At 3:30am Pete thinks we have a possum but I’m pretty sure it’s just another rat. We had put poison out and the electric traps with new batteries, but still hear him running around sometimes. OK Pete was right, it’s a possum!! I got out of bed to have a look.

We consulted the video cameras and he’d been drinking water from the watermelon and been up and down the tree a few times. I couldn’t wait until we were best friends!

No other visitors on Thurs morning, except some King Parrots eating our oranges before we’ve had a chance to!

It poured just as we were planning to go plant the new shrubs. So we spent some time trying to work out what to do about the meter boxes Pete wanted to order. There were 3 but only 2 were currently in stock. Delivery to us was something like $400 so we were looking at Cherrybrook or Mayfield as options. But at least 1 item was quite heavy and would arrive on a pallet, which complicated things a bit. Settled on Mayfield and we’ll try to co-ordinate to be there for the delivery and get it loaded straight into the Shark.

By that time it was 2:30 and the sun was out again, so we were heading down to plant. We got some things together and headed down to KoalaKorner in the Shark. I had some difficulty using the cameras to back through one of the gates as the pictures were a bit blurry / distorted.

After a bit of debate about the best spot to plant (I thought we would be planting them amongst the other plants, but Pete thought better down closer to the water) we got to work. Pete would drill holes, then we’d dig out the dirt, fill the hole with water, then plant.

We planted Osmanthus, Hibiscus Heterophyllus and Acacia Fimbriata.

Unfortunately we only got 5 done before it started to rain and it looked like it would get heavy - so we packed up and headed home. A couple of minutes later it absolutely chucked down. An hour down, only 5 shrubs planted and 25 to go haha

In the heavy rain, I noticed the pipe from the gutter to the tank was quite leaky - I think Pete tried to fix it later.

Sometime in the afternoon, Pete got this excellent shot of a lady Chipper -

More possum visits this evening!

Just bird visitors on Friday.

The passion fruit is flowering again - I thought it had been dying down for the winter. The watermelons are looking good.

Around 1:30 we headed into town. Saw a package in the letterbox as we were heading out - the new dash cam! Pete immediately started tearing into it and making a mess - at one point he accidentally tipped everything out on to the floor - not distracting at all!

We headed up to the lookout to see the nice clouds and rainbow - no Huey today though.

From the lookout we saw a side road and thought we might be able to drive down to the river, but when we got there the entrance looked like someone’s property - though it’s a proper tarred road with a street sign so I feel like they’ve just been sneaky and put a fence with their name on it to stop people driving down there! Looking on the map, the spot near the river that we were trying to get to is labelled “Old Bowman Farm Road - River public access” which definitely makes me think we should be able to access it.

Headed over to Dangar Rd to see how the owner-builder was getting on - there didn’t seem like there had been much progress since last time.

Stopped at Woolies and it was super busy and full of holidayers - not sure why! We parked out of the way over on the grass and a guy with a trailer still nearly ran into us. The expression on this doggo made us laugh -

IGA next and ran into one of the young workers from Woolies and she high-fived us - I think she must think we’re younger than we are hehe

Spotted some milk thistle weeds on the side of the IGA building and sneakily picked some to take home for the birds hehe

On our way into town, a small blue plant pot had flown out the back of the Shark as we were driving down Bundook Rd - luckily we found it and collected it on the way back!

Back home now - 3:30 and made some noodles for lunch and got back to work.

Spotted some super creepy fog on dusk - we went for a putt to see what it looked like from the house site - pretty cool!

On Saturday we had a Newcastle trip planned. I got up a bit after 8. I hadn’t slept very well and Pete hadn’t slept very long. I was feeling OK but then my belly got stirred up and we couldn’t leave until about 9:45.

First we visited Kevin at Choices Flooring in Heatherbrae after a recommendation from LMD. We had a bit of a look around while he served a couple of ladies who were trying to get a deal on carpet because they were running some charity. Pete and I were pretty agreed on what sort of flooring we’d like (Blackbutt - finally we agree on something haha) it’s just a matter of understanding what can work with our hydronic heating. We’d been told we can’t have proper wood, but hopefully we can have engineered board. Kevin wasn’t too sure but said he’d reach out to the manufacturers to get a better understanding and get back to us. He very generously let us borrow the sample.

Next we headed to the BYD dealer to pick up the floor mats - we weren’t too sure if we’d be able to get them as Pete originally got a text message saying it was fine, but we also had two emails - one saying it was fine, then one shortly after saying we’d have to go during the week -

We thought we’d chance our luck by just showing the favourable text message - we saw Thomas who had helped us with the Shark test drive, and he was happy to have a chat and have a look for us - luckily the mats had been set aside for us with an invoice already printed, so we made the payment and all was good, woohoo!

Next we headed to Winnings to discuss kitchen appliances. It was hard to find parking. We drove around the block then found a carpark but the spots were too small so we kept looking out on the street. I had to turn around in one of the streets, and when I was reversing I put my foot too hard on the accelerator and it shot back until I braked heavily - Pete reckons I left tyre marks! It was all very stressful and I was over it! Electric vehicles accelerate faster than petrol cars because their electric motors deliver 100% of their maximum torque instantly from a dead stop - just something I still have to get a bit more used to.

We met Keryn at Winnings and Pete took her through his wishlist so we could get some quotes together. It was the first time I was hearing some of these numbers and I needed a lie down haha

On the plus side, at least delivery was free hahaha

Next we headed to Beaumont St to get a schnitty wrap for lunch. Then we drove over to Gerros - arrived about 2:30, ate lunch and caught up. I got a surprise gift - a cute doggo pot! Pete spent some time installing the new car mats, they looked pretty schmick.

V&B said they’ll visit for a couple of nights, in a couple of weeks once things have calmed down at home. Liam joked that he’d visit on Wednesday so he could write his name in our freshly poured concrete haha

Pete and I headed off for our next errands - petrol, Coles and Bunnings. I was confused about why Pete was directing me to the Bunnings that was out of the way instead of the one on the way home, but as it turned out it was only about 13mins difference so not too bad.

Pete bought a new drill bit for the auger, so we can drill bigger holes for the shrubs. I had $200 cash from some money Mum had given me last year that I hadn’t got around to spending yet, and I wanted to get a few things for the garden. Firstly some shears like Dad’s that I’d borrowed when they last visited. Then a few herbs. I’d collected a bunch of things then Pete got a price check done - $165.60 - we very carefully calculated the next items but somehow when we got to the till we were 18c over! So embarrassing. I was momentarily panicked because I thought I didn’t have any more money, but then I remembered we could just pay the rest on card haha but then I found another $5 so that worked out better. We ended up with the shears, a 10-pack of snapdragon seedlings, a Fittonia plant, a Callisia Pink Panther, some Allium bulbs, 2 punnets of strawberries, cauliflower, coriander, parsley, rocket and 1 Chinese cabbage.

Pete did a magic job fitting everything into one box and securing it in the back of the Shark. While he was doing that, a man walked past and commented how good the Shark looks in orange hehe

Got some KFC on the way home - a man in a Roosters shirt (top bloke) commented on Pete’s shorts.

It was quite an eventful trip down the Bucketts - we saw a wallaby, some deer and a cat!

Here is a time lapse of the dash cam footage from our trip -

And here are my attempts at getting stills of the critters we saw hehe -

The dash cam isn’t quite right yet but Pete’s working on it.

We thought we might see the possum when we got home, but Pete thinks he’d hiding in the roof because it’s been raining. We later saw that he’d been playing Extreme Possum Warrior while we were out haha

All the plants made it home OK, due to Pete’s expert boxing/strapping and my expert driving hahaha

On Sunday morning, I noticed some grass is finally shooting up in the dirt patches out the front - Pete had tried all sorts of things to get grass to grow there but we’d pretty much given up - not sure why it’s changed its mind now!

We prepared to plant some more of the shrubs. Armed with Pete’s new auger bit, I was hopeful it was going to be a bit easier today at least.

I also realised it was a good opportunity to plant a few of the things that had been sitting on the porch for months because we didn’t know where to plant them. I drove the buggy around so I could load them up and wouldn’t have to carry them to the Shark - win!

I sat in the buggy while I waited for Pete to have his shower, and Willie sang me a song.

When Pete got out, we finished loading the Shark because I’d done a terrible job (forgot the little spade and the water) then headed down.

Pete got the auger going and it was making a racket - a few moments later I spotted a big Blue Tongue Lizard running for his life, he must have wondered what the heck was happening haha poor fella.

The new auger was much better at digging wider and deeper holes, yay.

Pete stood on one of the plants I’d just planted :(

We planted the Bottlebrush, the Gum and the Peach tree and most of the shrubs before we ran out of water. One of the new shrubs was ‘Pultenea’ which Google tells me should have lovely yellow flowers.
